Improved EE performance behavior by removing old iPSX2 diagnostic overhead from hot emulation paths. Overall emulator performance is now improved, and device heat may be improved as well. 

Various games have received corrected graphics thanks to @Dib1998 VU fix in 1.2.4

Fixed custom PNG texture replacements appearing too dark on iOS thanks to @yuliangtao

Updated app and OSD version display to ARMSX2 iOS 1.3.

Fixes from @J1coding 

Large imported files now use a safer fallback when the normal file copy path fails. Instead of loading the whole imported file into memory at once, the app now streams the file in small chunks through a temporary file before moving it into place. This should make large ISO, CHD, and other game imports less likely to hit memory problems on iOS.

BIOS imports now give clearer feedback when a copied BIOS-related file is not actually bootable. If a companion ROM or unsupported BIOS dump is imported, the app explains that it cannot be used to boot games instead of making the import look fully successful.

Game and BIOS imports now warn before replacing existing files with the same name. Cancelling keeps the current files untouched, while Replace imports the selected batch intentionally.

Cover download failures now give clearer guidance about what to check next. Local cover selection has also been improved: users can choose covers from Photos, and the Files picker now uses the same reliable picker flow as the game and BIOS import screens.

releases.name: ARMSX2-iOS 1.2
releases.body:
ARMSX2-iOS has been updated to version 1.2, here is what's changed:

GameDB support is now bundled directly into the app.

Built-in compatibility fixes can now load automatically for recognized games.

GameDB now shows a boot notification so testers know if a game was recognized.

GameDB status now distinguishes between loaded, game recognized, fixes applied, or no entry found.

Added safer iOS Metal handling for GameDB renderer fixes.

Fixed a crash path where GameDB could force a software-renderer FMV mode that does not play nicely with the iOS Metal build.

Added protection against aggressive GameDB graphics fixes breaking games on Metal.

Added global GameDB controls in Emulator settings.

Added separate toggles for GameDB Core Fixes and GameDB Graphics Fixes.
Added separate GameDB PNACH patch control so cheat/60 FPS patches are not tied to renderer fixes.

Added per-game GameDB Core Fixes and Graphics Fixes controls.
Users can now disable GameDB Graphics Fixes for only the games that look worse, while keeping GameDB enabled for games it improves.

Castlevania-style GameDB graphics fixes can stay enabled without forcing the same behavior on every game.

SoulCalibur-style regressions can now be worked around by disabling GameDB Graphics Fixes per game.

Added safer handling for GameDB native-scaling fixes on iOS.

Added extra GameDB/iOS renderer logging for tester reports.

Improved VM pause behavior when returning to the menu or opening runtime overlays.

Reduced the chance of menu/Q-menu audio stutter caused by the game continuing to run behind heavy overlays.

Added safer NVRAM/config saving behavior to avoid bad BIOS-path saves.

Overall GameDB is now useful without being all or nothing, you can use it to fix games while also disabling it when risky renderer fixes don't play nice with the game you are testing.

releases.name: ARMSX2-iOS 1.2.4
releases.body:
Fixed major Burnout Revenge graphics issues on iOS/Metal, including broken skybox rendering, bad scene artifacts, reflection glitches, and the glow issue! Other games benefit from this as well, GT4 is one example, so be sure to test!

Added @Dib1998 ARM64 VU fixes for Burnout, fixing reflections and the glow issue. 

Improved Burnout GameDB/GS hardware-fix handling so the right Burnout fixes apply without leaking unsafe settings into other games.

Fixed Metal blending behavior that affected Burnout and helped restore correct graphics output.

Importing unsupported game, BIOS, or PNACH files now gives clearer guidance, and important setup errors stay visible until you dismiss them instead of disappearing too quickly.

Memory card creation also has better validation, so empty names, invalid characters, and duplicate names are caught before the app tries to create the card.

Runtime failure messages for disc swapping and save/load states are now more helpful, and important in-game warnings stay visible longer while normal success messages remain brief.

releases.name: ARMSX2-iOS 1.2 hotfix
releases.body:
Hotfix based off testers feedback. GameDB stays enabled and working.
Fixed Compatibility Lab Off not fully disabling risky renderer fixes.
Fixed unsafe GameDB/manual GS hardware hacks still slipping through on iOS Metal.
Fixed getSkipCount still being applied even when compatibility fixes were disabled.
Fixed Guitar Hero III / SLUS-21672 rendering break caused by leftover GS hardware hacks.
iOS Metal now ignores unsafe graphics hacks when GameDB Graphics Fixes are disabled.
iOS Metal now clears stale per-game/manual renderer hacks that were saved from older builds.
Blocked risky renderer fixes such as getSkipCount, textureInsideRT, autoFlush, alignSprite, skipdraw, and aggressive native scaling when disabled.
GameDB metadata, serial/CRC detection, titles, covers, and patches remain available.
Added clearer logs so testers can confirm when iOS Metal is ignoring unsafe compatibility hacks.
Games that benefit from GameDB can still use it.
Games that break from GameDB graphics fixes can now disable only the risky graphics side without losing GameDB entirely.

### ARMSX2 1.0.8 Stable Changelog

ARMSX2 1.0.8 is now available as the latest stable release. This update brings major compatibility, graphics, performance, and usability improvements, with the biggest focus being vastly improved Mali GPU support from all the nighties since 1.0.6.

**Major Mali GPU Improvements**

Mali support has been significantly improved in ARMSX2 1.0.8. Mali users no longer need to rely on a separate Mali-specific build to benefit from recent graphics fixes and compatibility improvements. These fixes are now included directly in the main ARMSX2 build.

This update should improve the experience on Mali devices by reducing graphics issues, improving OpenGL behavior, and making more games playable or stable on affected hardware.

For testing on some Mali devices, users may need to set Blending to Maximum and disable Show GPU on Stats to avoid a black screen. This was tested on a Redmi 9 Prime with a Mali G52 MC2/MP2 GPU.

Please let us know whether these changes improve your experience on Mali devices. You can join our discord to connect with us! [https://discord.gg/KwAChKDctz](url)

**OpenGL Renderer Improvements**

The GL renderer has received major improvements, especially for devices affected by rendering bugs. These changes should improve both performance and compatibility across supported Android devices, with Mali devices seeing some of the most important benefits.

**HostFS Support**

This latest update also includes HostFS support, allowing supported homebrew and development workflows to access files from the host device more easily.

**VU1 Emulation Improvements**

VU1 emulation has also been improved. Games such as the GTA series should now play as expected, and other games affected by similar VU1-related issues may also be fixed.

**New Features**

- Added GPU Profile Override setting.
- Added support for disc swapping.
- Added FPS limit / framerate control.
- Added new internal resolution scale options: 0.25x, 0.5x, and 0.75x.
- Added a new on-screen display / OSD.
- Added support for creating memory cards from 8 MB to 64 MB.
- Added support for folder memory cards.
- Added a new option to disable unsafe OSD warnings.
- Added CHD cover support.
- Improved PNACH cheat importing so imported files are automatically renamed to the game’s serial CRC.
- Added automatic // handling when importing PNACH files.
- Fixed PNACH Android data location behavior, allowing cheats to be saved where the user wants.
- Fixed Fast Boot.
- Fixed Instant VU being disabled while MTVU is enabled.
- Fixed the Trilinear OSD bug.
- Fixed a fullscreen UI bug.
- Fixed a memory card section issue in the sw600dp layout.
- Included the latest fullscreen UI fix in the stable release.
- Boot Logo Update

ARMSX2 now includes an updated boot logo with sound, created by @Vivimagic and audio done by @jpolo1224. 

**Credits**

Huge thanks to @DIB1998 for the major Mali, OpenGL, OSD, resolution scale, memory card, disc swapping, FPS limit, and graphics-related improvements.

Thanks also to @momo-AUX1 for extensive bug fixing, new settings, and helping bring the Mali fixes into the main ARMSX2 build.

Thank you to @Vivimagic for the new ARMSX2 boot logo, and credits to (NASA/CXC/SAO/K.Arcand, SYSTEM Sounds (M. Russo, A. Santaguida) for the sound used as well. The 1987A Supernova Sonification just screams PS2. Also, to everyone testing nightly builds and reporting issues, as well as the rest of the ARMSX2 team for their continued contributions.

releases.name: Winlator Cmod v13.1.1
releases.body:
_Minor update v13.1.1 fixed custom icons, default renderer, and warning prompt handling on new installs_ 

------------------------------

-   **`evshim` Rewrite:** The entire controller shim (`libevshim.so`) has been rewritten, **completely eliminating the use of shared memory (`mmap`)**, resulting in a massive reduction in CPU overhead and a significant performance boost, especially on lower-end devices. Box64 3.2 and 3.6 are now compatible, and have been restored.

-   **ALSA-Reflector Improved** The pacer's ring buffer and reconnection logic have been refined, expect better performance and reliability.

-   **Universal CPU Overhead Reduction:** I've gone through the code to find and eliminate performance bottlenecks, once again, big thanks to @Pipetto-crypto as always for the guidance and his improvements to the Graphics Wrapper. 

### ✨ New Feature: VkBasalt Integration

-   **Per-Shortcut Sharpening & Effects:** Thanks to @Pipetto-crypto You can now enable VkBasalt on a per-shortcut basis to apply CAS and DLS to your games.

### 🐞 Stability & Bug Fixes:

This update includes a huge number of fixes for a smoother experience.

-   **Corrupted Shortcut Crash Fixed:** Implemented safety checks to prevent the app from crashing when parsing corrupted `.desktop` files.

-   **Proton & Frontend Fixes:** Resolved issues that caused crashes when launching the frontend or using XrActivity.

-   **Input Controls Fixed:** Corrected bugs with toggle switches and range buttons in the input controls overlay.

-   **Gyro Zeroing Improved:** The gyroscope now has better logic for finding its origin point, resulting in more responsive and accurate motion controls.

-   **Renderer Selection for DDraw:** Added a renderer selection option to fix black screens in older DDraw games, thanks to some last minute insight to **@Pipetto-Crypto**.

### ⚙️ Core & Asset Updates

-   **Proton 10 Support:** The codebase is now prepared for the next major Proton release. Stay tuned. (...and Wine 9.20)

-   **Updated Assets:** The default Box64, Proton packs, and other core assets have been updated with the latest fixes and improvements. Additional .wcp have been added to Contents: updated DXVK (+ Stripped, Sarek for lower end devices), updated VKD3D, and Turnip. Thank you @K11MCH1 for your excellent repository.

The list goes on actually. More planned as always- now get to testing! Spin up GTA IV and watch it fly! 🫡

-Alex

**WARNING: _Make new Containers_.** And if you were fast enough to get the apk within the first 5 minutes, please re-download it.

releases.name: Winlator Cmod v13: The Controller Revolution is Here! (And much more...)
releases.body: The wait is over. After months of work the next major evolution of Winlator Cmod has arrived. I teased that a controller revolution was coming, but the reality is so much bigger. This isn't just an update; it's a top-to-bottom overhaul focused on bringing a native, seamless gaming experience to your device. This release is the culmination of a journey, and I'm proud to share it with you. ✨ What's New in Cmod v13 ✨ -------------------------- ### 🎮 The Controller Revolution: Native Gamepad Support is Here! The old input methods are gone (sorta), replaced by a completely new, from-the-ground-up controller implementation built on a native SDL2 backend. - **Native XInput & DInput Support:** No more switching settings per game! Controllers are now treated like real controllers. If it works on a PC, it should just work here. - **Multiplayer (Up to 4 Players!):** You heard that right. Connect up to four controllers and they will be properly recognized as Player 1, 2, 3, and 4. - **Vibration / Rumble:** Feel the action with full haptic feedback support. It can be toggled on or off. - **Advanced Motion Controls (Gyro):** A completely revamped and customizable gyroscope implementation. Map it to the left or right stick, fine-tune sensitivity, deadzone, and smoothing, and set an activation button. - **Turbo & Macros:** Set up autofire for any button (including triggers!) for each of your controllers. - **Virtual Gamepad Enhancements:** The on-screen controls are now more responsive than ever, with reactive visual feedback to show when a button is pressed. ### 🔊 ALSA-Reflector: The Unbreakable Audio Engine So- you're in a game, you connect your Bluetooth headphones or a phone call comes in, and the audio dies, forcing a restart. **Those days are over.** - **Introducing "ALSA-Reflector":** A new, optional audio driver that creates a virtual, unbreakable audio sink. It provides stable back-pressure to Wine, completely immune to Android's device changes. - **Seamless Recovery:** Real audio is mirrored to your hardware. If the connection breaks, the playback stream is automatically rebuilt in the background without interrupting the game's audio flow. The music never stops. (Well... it might, it's a work in progress!) ### 🚀 Core System & Proton Enhancements - **Bionic Native Libs:** Thanks to **@Pipetto-Crypto**, Winlator Cmod now uses native Bionic libraries. ### 🎨 UI & Quality-of-Life Tsunami - **Favorite Shortcut Launcher:** See that new star icon in the toolbar? Set your favorite game shortcut and launch it with a single tap from the main screen. - **"Disable Touchscreen Mouse" Option:** You can now completely disable the touchscreen as a mouse input device when using a virtual gamepad. - **Countless Fixes:** From custom shortcut icons and `.lnk` file parsing to a smarter app shutdown process and dozens of UI polish updates, nearly every corner of the app has been refined. The Journey & Thank You ----------------------- This release absolutely would not have been possible alone. - A massive thank you to **@Pipetto-crypto** for his phenomenal work on the graphics wrappers, Bionic native libraries, for taking the time to teach me the intricacies of compiling bionic native libraries, and for keeping the Cmod torch lit while I was on break. - To **@K11MCH1** for pushing me to learn how to compile Bionic libs in the first place and [his excellent videos,](https://www.youtube.com/@Zerokimchii) and the entire **EmuGear Discord community**: Your endless testing, feedback, bug reports, and encouragement were the fuel for this entire project. You guys make this all worth it. - And finally, a shout-out to my digital homies Gemini and GPT. For the countless late-night debugging sessions, untangling the multithreaded madness of the ALSA-Reflector, and providing the sanity checks I needed that kept this project on the rails---I genuinely couldn't have done it without you. This release is for all of you. Now, go play some games! *Alex* *ps: I'll write some helpful release notes tomorrow... time to rest haha...* **ALSO - IMPORTANT: CONTROLLERS REQUIRE NORMAL OR ESSENTIAL START-UP FOR SERVICES!** And box64 MUST be 3.7- it's a special patched version. Working on that next!

releases.name: MangoHud for Winlator Glibc - Fixed** GPU/CPU stats
releases.body:
Huge thanks to @hisham2630 of DarkOS for providing the source code for his implementation for certain hardware stats, which made this release possible (or significantly faster).

---

### Notes:
- **Battery Stats:** Requires root access and SELinux enforcement disabled. Other stats do not require root access.**
- **Limitations:** I/O RW is not implemented, and some features might not work on Android.
- **Fork:** Source code will be available on my MangoHub repo for contributions as soon as I prepare it.
- **Compatibility:** Currently works only with Glibc environments. **GPU Load on the Adreno a618 and a619 is currently not supported.
- **OpenGL:** _Can_ be enabled with `MANGOHUD_DLSYM` however, I cannot get it working in my testing. If you get different results, let me know. 
---

### Installation Instructions:

1. Set the following environment variables in your Winlator container settings:
   - `MANGOHUD=1`
   - _Optionally_: `MANGOHUD_CONFIG=engine_version,gpu_temp,fps,frametime,ram,vulkan_driver,arch`
     *(You can customize these. See [MangoHud Parameters](https://github.com/flightlessmango/MangoHud))*.

2. Download and unzip `Winlator_Mangohud_Glibc_Release.zip` somewhere on your storage.

3. Launch a _Glibc_ 😉 container, and Run the provided `install_mangohud.bat`:
   - This will merge the `usr` directory with the existing `usr` directory in Wine's Z: drive.

4. Alternatively:
   - Copy the `usr` directory manually to your Wine Z:/ drive and merge it.

5. You're all set! Launch your Wine application to enjoy MangoHud overlays.

This will be included by default in the next Winlator Cmod release.

---

releases.name: Winlator Corefonts Pack (Fixes Steam UI, Epic Games Launcher, and others in Winlator Glibc)
releases.body:
While I continue working on Cmod V12 and my implementation of Winetricks I've got a little surprise.  This pack will fix the UI issues in Steam, Epic Games Launcher, and others. Follow the instructions per the folder names, or read this short guide:

1. Download the Winlator Corefonts Pack.zip
2. Extract it
3. Launch a 9.2 container in Cmod, Amod, or Frost, (might work in others idk - but it must be Winlator Glibc)
4. Copy the contents of folder 1 directly to Drive Z, (the home, usr, and opt directories)
5. Import the registry files I included from Folder 2 by going to Start Menu \ System Tools \ Registry Editor, then File \ Import Registry File and import the files, 1.reg, 2.reg, and 3.reg
6. Launch Steam

(Step 3 and 4 are optional if you have issues)

releases.name: Wine 9.2 from Winlator 8.0r1 for Glibc - BrunoSX latest commits + Longjunyu2 Xinput/Dinput
releases.body:
This is Bruno's latest commits from his wine-custom repo for Winlator 8.0, but recompiled to work on Glibc. This means it contains the latest Winlator 8.0 patches and workarounds (except for his Xinput/Dinput implementation, as that won't work without changes to Winlator itself). It will likely be the included default in  Cmod v12. In the meantime, I've been able to run a few games that would not work without this Wine specifically. Make sure to add the following Environmental Variables:

**Key = Value**

WINEFORCENTCONTINUE = 1
WINEVMEMMAXSIZE = 16384 

There are a few other env vars worth looking into but games I've tested successfully so far:

**Deus Ex - Mankind Divided** (DX12 only, requires WINEVMEMMAXSIZE)
**GRIP: Combat Racing** - Requires (WINEFORCENTCONTINUE)
**Need for Speed ProStreet** - Fixes the UI in the menu by default

There are I'm sure plenty of more games/apps to be tested. But think of this as a preview of things to come. 

Other features added to wine:

Restart/Reconfigure Container via Start Menu
WINEOVERRIDEAFFINITYMASK which I haven't quite figured out how to use yet, but it forces the task affinity to a value you set
WINVERSION forces the selected windows version as Wine's current default, such as "winxp" or "win7"

I will push the source code for this to my wine-custom forked repo. In the meantime, you can download the .wcp here!

releases.name: Winlator 7.1.3x Cmod GLIBC v10 - Compatibility Fixes! Screen Effects! Toon Shader! Import/Export Containers! Box64 Version Switching! Bugfixes and more!
releases.body:
I've reverse engineered the new Screen Effects feature from Winlator 8.0 and added one of my own, a simple ToonShader! I'm very happy with the results. This means you now get Brightness/Contrast/Gamma controls, FXAA, and CRT screen filters as well. I've made a lot of changes to the Wine prefix, making this more of an Amod/Frost hybrid. I've also made some tweaks of my own, to fix issues with Mono and Gecko, like adding in an override for mscorre. This release also includes an offline installer for Mono and Gecko in the Runtime Libraries section of the start menu. I can't directly port over every new feature from Winlator 8.0 yet, but when Bruno releases the source code I will try my best. Which is why this remains 7.1.3. I call it 7.1.3x because it's basically a halfway point to 8.0, and still going by Longjunyu2's numbering scheme for Glibc specific changes.

However, this prefix I can guarantee a couple of major fixes, namely, no more UE4 Fatal Error for some games. Halo MCC is working! Fixes for FMV's in some titles. No more .Net warnings for new containers when Mono and Gecko are installed. I've also made a bug fixes to existing features of Cmod. I really think this is solid build. This is now a full on Frost/Amod hybrid! You'll get best results with new containers, in my experience, but start menu and prefix tweaks should still apply to existing containers to an extent. 

**Added:**
-DXVK 2.4.1 and 2.4.1-gplasync built-in
-Screen Effects (Brightness controls, FXAA, CRT) from Winlator 8.0!
-ToonShader for ScreenEffects  
-Import and Export containers! For recovering containers, or importing a friend's! 
-Box64 Version Switching for shortcuts! Ignore the "2.7" when you first open a new shortcut, it goes by preferences in Setting until you set it yourself.
-Modified custom Wine - with optimizations from Frost Glibc, but merged with Amod hybrid, resulting in what you might call, AFCMod. lol. This brings Flash Player, Windows Media Player, Registry tweaks, and other neat additions
-ReactOS App Store shortcut is now functional. TBH I didn't even know this was a thing until this week!
-Offline installers for Mono and Gecko added to "4-Runtime Libraries" in start menu. 
-Container Launching UI is adopted from Winlator 8.0

**Fixes:**
-No more UE4 Fatal Errors! Halo Master Chief Collection is working!
-Fixed Green screen for FMVs in some titles
-mscoree set to built-in then native, applied by default for new containers, correcting some issues with .net framework games and apps like HedgeModManager. Meaning, full support for Sonic Generations D3D11 Mod
-Fixed long text re-sizing for game titles in Big Picture Mode 
-Fixed issues with Frontend Export path needing to be resaved every time you close and re-open the app
-Fixed Dark Mode theme sometimes randomly switching off half-way leaving a broken light theme interface until app restart
-many other changes and tweaks that I once again can't remember...

**Still upcoming:**
-Better menu control for Big Picture Mode when using a controller
-Background music for BPM
-Custom wallpaper for BPM
-Settings changes in BPM
-Custom game icons 
-Hopefully reactive buttons for input controls from Winlator 8.0, though I may have to dissect some .smali 

The source code is not up yet, as I use it to port my changes to Proot. I will of course upload it so others can adopt in the near future! As always, let me know of bugs and things via discord or other means and I'll see what I can do!

releases.name: v2.5: DCNet, new on-screen gamepad, DreamConn+ and DreamPicoPort adapters
releases.body:
## What's Changed
* DCNet: a free dedicated VPN service for Dreamcast games that only needs a basic Internet connection. 30 game servers are already available and more are coming.
* Improved on-screen gamepad for Android and iOS: move and resize controls, custom designs, arcade-specific layout, unused controls hidden based on game (arcade) or device (console games).
* Support for physical Dreamcast controllers with DreamConn+ and DreamPicoPort adapters: gamepad, VMU, vibration pack and more.
* New Dreamcast "Full Controller" with 2 analog axes and all possible buttons (Panther DC controller).
* Better analog axis emulation when using a keyboard or digital buttons by using a ramp up/down curve.
* Hardware CD/DVD/BD-ROM support
* GD-ROM arcade games load time reduced to zero.
* Improved GD-ROM access time, particularly with HLE BIOS.
* Fixed: Vulkan per-pixel mode on Mali GPUs.
* Work-around an OpenGLES bug in many drivers displaying the game screen upside down.
* Per-game VMU now compatible with multidisk games.
* Support for some encrypted cheats.
* Online support for Hundred Swords, PBA Bowling, StarLancer and The Next Tetris.

releases.name: Bannerlator 3.0.4
releases.body: # Bannerlator 3.0.4 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **3.0.4 is the Steam update.** The app's Steam client has been rebuilt from the ground up as a native engine — sign-in, library, downloads, cloud saves, achievements, friends and chat now all run on it — and the SteamLite online/VAC launcher got the fixes and polish that make real-Steam games launch reliably: no more "Incorrect Version" / "could not connect to Steam" on launch, a pre-flight check before the container opens, and a Friends tab right in the in-game drawer. As always the update is **entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall** — so your containers, Wine installs, themes, accent colour and per-game settings all carry over untouched. Install straight over 3.0.3. > **SteamLite users:** the launch popup will ask you to update the SteamLite client package (v4 or newer) before the first online launch — one tap, then Launch. Verified on this build: Counter-Strike: Source on a VAC-secured server, Stumble Guys online (including its game update through the new engine), Brawlhalla online. # What's New — everything since 3.0.3 ## 🦀 Native Steam engine *(new — on by default)* - **The Steam client inside the app is now a native engine** instead of the Java one inherited from GameNative. Sign-in (QR and password/Steam Guard), your owned library, depot downloads with resume and verify, beta branches, cloud saves, achievements, rich presence, friends, chat and presence all run on it. - **Faster, lighter, more resilient** — a single hardened session that self-heals on reconnect, with less memory and battery overhead than the Java stack. - **Steam connection region** setting — pick the Steam region the app connects through (Settings → Steam), useful on networks where the auto-picked servers misbehave. - The Java engine stays available for one release as a fallback: Log Manager → **"Native Steam engine (restart required)"**. If anything Steam-related misbehaves for you, flip it off, restart, and please send the SteamLite/Steam logs. The Java engine is scheduled for removal in the next release. - Every new Steam control has a **?** help button explaining what it does. ## 🎮 SteamLite (real Steam · online · VAC) — reliability - **Fixed: "Incorrect Version, Please Update" / "Could not connect to Steam servers" on launch** (Brawlhalla and others). Steam allows one login per account; the app now pauses its own Steam session right before the container opens and resumes it when the game exits, so the game's login is never kicked. - **Cloud saves sync *before* the container opens** — the pre-launch cloud pull now finishes first, then the hand-off happens. - **Pre-flight before launch** — a small "Getting Steam ready" popup (photo slideshow) while the app checks sign-in, cloud, game files, the SteamLite client and your **network / NAT type**, so a bad network is called out before the game starts instead of failing inside it. - **Fixed an intermittent crash at game start** caused by Steam's overlay injecting into the game process; overlay injection is now disabled for SteamLite launches. - **VAC-aware launching** — secure (VAC) launch is used when the game needs it, with a per-game override; non-VAC games start faster. - **Live agent channel** — the app and the in-container Steam agent now talk directly instead of guessing from log files, so launch status and errors are exact. - **Update & Launch** — when a newer SteamLite client package is available, the launch popup shows it and installs it in one tap before launching. - Better crash diagnostics in the SteamLite log bundle (crash cause quoted at the top, engine section, network verdict). - **Faster fallback for non-VAC titles** — when Steam accepts the launch but never spawns the game, non-VAC titles now start directly after ~15 s instead of ~60 s. > ⚠️ **Known issue (64-bit titles launched directly by Steam):** on some 64-bit games Steam's own spawn can still crash at startup with the overlay-injection signature; the launcher then starts the game directly. Non-VAC games (e.g. Stumble Guys) play online normally this way. A 64-bit **VAC** game that Steam launches directly would end up in an insecure start and be rejected by VAC servers — titles that go through a 32-bit launcher (Counter-Strike: Source, Team Fortress 2, Left 4 Dead 2) are unaffected. Fix in progress. ## 👥 Friends & chat while you play - **Friends tab in the in-game side drawer** — see who's online and chat without leaving the game. Populated by the app's session for normal launches and relayed through the SteamLite agent for real-Steam launches (Steam's headless session doesn't stream presence, so statuses there may show as "last known"). - Steam chat notifications setting is shared between Settings and the Friends page cog — one switch, no conflict. ## 📦 GOG - **DLC auto-detect + batch extract** — Fast Extract and the Unpack Archive screen now spot sibling `setup_*.exe` DLC installers next to a GOG base game and extract base + DLC into one merged folder in a single pass. ## 🧰 Project - Every pull request is now compiled against `main` by CI before it can be merged. ## 🗂️ New sister app — BFE (file explorer) **[github.com/The412Banner/BFE](https://github.com/The412Banner/BFE)** · latest **[v0.10](https://github.com/The412Banner/BFE/releases/latest)** · sideload-only, GPL-3.0 Bannerlator's built-in File Manager and its native extraction engine, lifted into a standalone Android file explorer for managing game files outside the emulator. What it does: - **Dual-pane commander** — two panes side by side, one shared toolbar; copy / move / rename / delete / share with multi-select, sort, search, grid or list. - **Every storage you have** — internal, SD card and USB, pinnable app-private folders via Android's storage picker, and **root browsing** on rooted devices. - **FitGirl and DODI repack extraction** — unpacks the repack's `setup.exe` + `Setup-N.bin` volumes natively (FreeArc / ISDone decoding on-device), no PC or Windows installer run needed. - **GOG offline installer extraction** — the `setup_.exe` installer is unpacked straight to game files, and **DLC installers sitting next to it are detected and extracted into the same game folder automatically** in one pass. - **Archives and disc images** — 7z, zip, rar (multi-part), tar / gz / xz, zst, split volumes, `.iso` / `.udf` / `.img`, `.wcp` / `.tzst` — the same extraction engine Bannerlator uses. - **Compress** folders back to `.wcp` / `.tzst` for sharing or importing into Bannerlator. - **APK cloner + signer** — duplicate an APK under a new package name and sign it, on device. - **Convert video to MP4** (bundled ffmpeg), plus New file / New folder, APK icons in listings. Early 0.x builds — please report anything odd on the BFE issue tracker. --- ## 🙏 Credits Built on the work of many open-source projects and their communities: - **Native Steam engine & SteamLite agent** — derived from **WinNative**'s GPL `wnsteam` client and `wn-steam-launcher` (hardened, extended and rebranded here); protocol groundwork from **SteamKit2** (the **SteamRE** team). - **Steam (fallback engine)** — **JavaSteam** (joshuatam's fork of **SteamKit2**) and **Goldberg / gbe_fork** (Detanup01 & contributors). - **Graphics & Frame Generation** — **DXVK** (Philip Rebohle & contributors), **VKD3D-Proton** (Hans-Kristian Arntzen & contributors), **Mesa / Turnip** (the Freedreno & Mesa teams), and **AMD FidelityFX (FSR)**. - **Containers, launch & runtime** — **Wine** (WineHQ) and **Proton / GE-Proton** (Valve & GloriousEggroll); **box64** (ptitSeb) and **FEXCore** (the FEX-Emu team). - **Audio** — Android **AAudio**, driven by our own **DirectAudio** endpoint. - **The app itself** — **Winlator** (brunodev85) and its Cmod lineage; **GameNative** (GPL-3.0) for the Steam session-hardening and present paths. *Steam is a trademark of Valve Corporation; other names are trademarks of their respective owners. Bannerlator is an independent project — not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them. Each component remains under its own license.*

releases.name: Bannerlator 3.0.3
releases.body: # Bannerlator 3.0.3 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **3.0.3 is a controls-focused update on top of 3.0.2** — a redesigned Input Controls screen that keeps your on-screen touch controls and your physical controllers as separate profile lanes, a visual Test & Bind tool for real pads, live layout previews, and opt-in microphone support for in-game voice — plus Steam, graphics and UI fixes. As always the update is **entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall** — so your containers, Wine installs, themes, accent colour and per-game settings all carry over untouched. Install straight over 3.0.2. # What's New — everything since 3.0.2 ## 🎮 Input Controls, redesigned - **On-screen and physical controllers now have separate profile lanes.** Your touch overlay and your real controller's button mapping are chosen independently — set a touch layout for the screen and a completely different mapping for the pad, and they run side by side without fighting each other. - **Redesigned, tabbed settings screen** — the old single long scroll is now a pinned profile bar over four focused tabs: **On-Screen · Controller · Assign · Device**. Profile badges show at a glance whether a profile carries a touch layout, controller bindings, or both. - **Visual Test & Bind for physical controllers** — an accurate picture of your pad that lights up as you press each button, stick and trigger; tap any button to remap it, and confirm every input registers. Available from Settings and in-game (renamed **"Physical Controller Test / Bind"**). - **Live on-screen layout preview** — selecting a touch profile shows its actual overlay right in the settings screen; tap it to jump straight into the editor. - **Per-pad battery level and a test-rumble button** for each connected controller. - Reliability fixes so **D-pad and stick remaps take effect immediately** and **binding edits apply without a manual Reset Input**. ## 🎙️ Microphone support — DirectAudio *(new — off by default)* - Opt-in **in-game microphone capture** through DirectAudio, so games and apps that use voice (party chat, push-to-talk, voice commands) can hear your mic. Enable it per container or per game — it's off by default, so nothing changes unless you turn it on. ## 🧰 Launch & updates - **Verify / Check-for-updates** row on the launch popup for Steam games — check whether a game is up to date and update it on demand, without anything being applied automatically. - The launch menu now **fits and scrolls cleanly in landscape**, with the Launch button kept pinned. ## 🏪 Steam & downloads - **Cancel & delete** for a wedged Steam download — a guaranteed reset that clears a stuck download so you can start clean. - **Security:** Steam credentials are now scrubbed from Community Config export, details and apply, so a shared config can't leak your sign-in. ## 🎞️ Graphics - Frame-generation capture fix (256 MB shard sizing) for the Win-FG pipeline. ## 🖥️ Components & UI - **Content packs only** in the component browser — cleaner browsing that hides bare archives (GPU Drivers and release-tagged items excepted). - **WIN Components** screen refined for landscape — GPU Drivers promoted to their own category with a single install path, a wide two-column download-speed dialog, and a more compact layout. - Games grid tile sizing fixed in landscape. --- ## 🙏 Credits Built on the work of many open-source projects and their communities: - **Microphone / audio** — Android **AAudio**, driven by our own **DirectAudio** endpoint. - **Graphics & Frame Generation** — **DXVK** (Philip Rebohle & contributors), **VKD3D-Proton** (Hans-Kristian Arntzen & contributors), **Mesa / Turnip** (the Freedreno & Mesa teams), and **AMD FidelityFX (FSR)**. - **Containers, launch & runtime** — **Wine** (WineHQ) and **Proton / GE-Proton** (Valve & GloriousEggroll); **box64** (ptitSeb) and **FEXCore** (the FEX-Emu team). - **Steam** — **JavaSteam** (joshuatam's fork of **SteamKit2** by the **SteamRE** team) and **Goldberg / gbe_fork** (Detanup01 & contributors). - **The app itself** — **Winlator** (brunodev85) and its Cmod lineage. *Steam is a trademark of Valve Corporation; other names are trademarks of their respective owners. Bannerlator is an independent project — not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them. Each component remains under its own license.*

releases.name: Bannerlator 3.0.2
releases.body: # Bannerlator 3.0.2 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **3.0.2 is a Steam-focused update on top of 3.0.1** — Friends & Chat, real-Steam (VAC) online play, achievements & cloud saves, one-touch save syncing and SD-card installs, plus graphics/frame-gen and runtime polish. As always the update is **entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall** — so your containers, Wine installs, themes, accent colour and per-game settings all carry over untouched. Install straight over 3.0.1. # What's New — everything since 3.0.1 ## 🖥️ Steam Friends & Chat *(new — off by default)* - Friends list with live presence (online / in-game / away), unread badges, collapsible sections. - Per-friend chat with text and **images**, persisted history, opens at the newest/first-unread message. - Add friends by code, name search, or quick-invite link; pending requests to accept/decline. - In-app friend profile, landscape two-pane view, chat notifications with a sound toggle, typing indicators, instant reconnect after a background drop. - 🙏 Special thanks to **iamtooshaar** (Discord) for helping test and work out the bugs in Steam Friends & Chat. ## 🔐 SteamLite — Real Steam (VAC) online *(new)* - A launch mode that runs your games through the **real Steam client** for a genuine, VAC-eligible session. - Watches the launcher exe (not the arch-specific `_win64`) so a game launches secure regardless of which exe the shortcut names. - In-game gold achievement pill for real-Steam unlocks; opt-in scrubbed log capture for diagnosing launches. - **SteamLite package:** [Real Steam / VAC — `steamlite-v1`](https://github.com/The412Banner/winlator-contents/releases/tag/steamlite-v1) — the genuine Steam client plus a clean-room headless agent (installed in-app). - **Verified working online** (device-proven, real account + secure launch on live VAC / live-service servers): **Counter-Strike 1.6**, **Counter-Strike: Source**, **Team Fortress 2**, **Left 4 Dead 2** (all VAC-secured), **Brawlhalla** and **Stumble Guys** (live-service matchmaking). *In testing:* **Borderlands 2**. ## 🏆 Achievements & Cloud Saves *(new)* - Real Steam achievements seeded from your account — tabbed detail page with an achievements grid, plus in-game gold pills as you unlock them. - **Works in both launch modes** — achievements unlock **and** sync whether you play through **Goldberg** (emulated Steam) or **SteamLite** (real Steam / VAC); your unlocks and cloud saves carry across either path. - Automatic cloud-save parity — saves sync to Steam Cloud around play sessions. - **NEW — one-touch “Sync Now”:** when the Save Manager flags games that need syncing, a single button on the banner syncs them **all at once**, each in the correct direction (upload what's newer locally, pull what's newer in the cloud), with a live “Syncing 3/7…” count — no more tapping every game one by one. - Goldberg achievement schema generation + version-check/update; fixed a silent no-op so achievements and cloud triggers actually fire. > ⚠️ **Steam save sync & achievements — use at your own risk.** These run through **third-party systems** (Valve's Steam and Goldberg), exactly like the store sign-ins. They depend on your connection: an **unstable or dropped internet connection or network — while downloading (syncing saves, achievements or games) or uploading — can leave data un-synced, incomplete or out of date**. It is **your responsibility** to ensure a proper, stable connection and to complete the sync/download/upload when required; verify it finished before relying on it across devices. ## 💾 Install to SD card *(new)* - Per-game toggle to install a Steam download onto a removable SD card to free internal space; the shortcut resolves via a container drive letter so secure launch, saves and achievements are unaffected. ## 🏪 Steam Store, Downloads & DLC - **Rebuilt game detail pages** — the Steam store's per-game screen was redesigned into a cleaner, landscape-aware tabbed layout (overview, achievements grid, DLC), with the store badge, connection state and launch actions together in one place. - STEAM store badge on tiles & rows, a live connection pill, and auto-connect on launch; download hardening and full owned-DLC listing. ## 🎞️ Graphics & Frame Generation - Frame-gen freeze fixes — a fuller pause/teardown/resume reset on level/model/preset change, a swapchain-recreate config reload, and an Adreno-840 present-id freeze fix; plus in-app frame-gen diagnostics. ## 🎛️ Containers, Launch & File Manager - **DXVK HUD off by default** on new containers (still toggleable in the env-var editor). - Launch-popup redesign (source- and orientation-adaptive), CUSTOM origin badge for games you add yourself, and file attributes (Read-only / Hidden) in the File Manager. ## 🔧 Chat & presence fixes - Chat history no longer wipes (server history merged, not replaced); images/messages no longer send twice; clipboard Paste; keyboard no longer covers the latest messages; friends no longer wipe to Offline on re-entry. --- ## 🙏 Credits Built on the work of many open-source projects and their communities: - **Steam friends / chat / store / downloads** — **JavaSteam** (joshuatam's fork), the Java port of **SteamKit2** by the **SteamRE** team. - **Real-Steam (VAC) online** — genuine **Steam client** components by **Valve**, driven headless by our own clean-room agent. - **Achievements & Cloud** — **Goldberg / gbe_fork** (Detanup01 & contributors). - **Graphics & Frame Generation** — **DXVK** (Philip Rebohle & contributors), **VKD3D-Proton** (Hans-Kristian Arntzen & contributors), **Mesa / Turnip** (the Freedreno & Mesa teams), **AMD FidelityFX (FSR)** + **RIFE**, and **lsfg-vk / Lossless Scaling**. - **Containers, launch & runtime** — **Wine** (WineHQ) and **Proton / GE-Proton** (Valve & GloriousEggroll); **box64** (ptitSeb) and **FEXCore** (the FEX-Emu team). - **The app itself** — **Winlator** (brunodev85) and its Cmod lineage. *Steam is a trademark of Valve Corporation; other names are trademarks of their respective owners. Bannerlator is an independent project — not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them. Each component remains under its own license.*

releases.name: Bannerlator 3.0.1
releases.body:
# Bannerlator 3.0.1 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **3.0.1 is a point release on top of 3.0.0** — two touch/display features built for foldables and handhelds, a reliability fix for large Steam downloads, plus file-manager and stability fixes. As always the update is **entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall** — so your containers, Wine installs, themes, accent colour and per-game settings all carry over untouched. Install straight over 3.0.0. # What's New — everything since 3.0.0 ## 🎮 Swipeable on-screen controls - **Slide onto a button to press it.** A finger sliding onto a button — even one that started on empty space and was moving the mouse — now presses it, so you can **roll across the D-pad** and **chain face buttons without lifting**. Sliding off releases it again. - **Slide-to-engage sticks.** Optionally grab an on-screen stick by sliding a finger onto it, with no separate tap. - **Your call, per control.** Mark any button or D-pad **Swipeable** in the controls editor, and flip swipe on/off **live per category** — Buttons / D-pad / Sticks — from a new **Swipe** tab in the in-game side menu. Defaults: Buttons on, D-pad and Sticks off. ## 🖥️ Foldable Screen Alignment — handheld split - **A game screen up top, a gamepad below.** On square-ish foldable inner displays, set **Screen Alignment** to **Top** or **Bottom**: the game runs in one half of the panel at a normal size while the on-screen controls get the **other half at full size** — like a handheld with a screen and a proper controller. - **Every fullscreen mode stays in its half.** Fit / Fill / Stretch / Integer all scale the game **inside** its half and never spill over the controls. - **Per-container or per-game**, and **live-toggleable** in the in-game side menu. **Center is unchanged**, so normal phones and handhelds behave exactly as before. ## 🎞️ Frame-generation flicker + FPS-drop fix - **Smoother Lossless Scaling frame generation.** Fixed the **black-frame flicker** and the **spurty FPS drops** that could appear after changing the frame-generation multiplier in-game (the lsfg-vk path) — switching multipliers now stays clean, no background/foreground bounce needed. ## 🛒 Steam — big downloads no longer run out of memory (#408) - **Large games download reliably.** Steam downloads now **spool to disk** instead of holding chunks in memory, so very large titles (e.g. an 87 GB game) download in full without an out-of-memory crash. The download engine is now also **vendored in-app**, so builds no longer depend on an external package server. ## 🗂️ Files, installs & fixes - **File Manager (grid view)** — grid tiles now open the same long-press **context menu** the list view has, plus a **"Select"** multi-select bar. And **extraction progress is honest** — GOG / Inno (innoextract) installs show real progress instead of a sawtoothing bar. *(the sawtoothing-progress bug was spotted by **Yurim** — thanks!)* - **Unpack ETA** — the minimized unpack pill now shows a live **ETA** alongside the percentage and speed. - **Vibration crash fixed** — dragging the in-game vibration slider to **0** while a controller was rumbling no longer crashes. *(reported by **noSkyWick** — thanks!)* - **arm64ec download sheet fixed** — on arm64ec containers, the shortcut editor's Advanced download button now opens the correct **WOWBox64** sheet instead of the Box64 one. ---

 

## 🙏 Credits & licenses Bannerlator is distributed under **GPL-3.0**; the complete, authoritative attribution list — including the **MIT Winlator lineage (© 2023 BrunoSX)** this app descends from — lives in **[THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/blob/main/THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md)**. Credits for the features in this release: - **🎮 Swipeable on-screen controls** — ported from **WinNative**, faithful to its per-control "Swipeable" behaviour, onto Bannerlator's **Winlator / Star** input lineage (**MIT © 2023 BrunoSX** — brunodev85, coffincolors, Pipetto-crypto, jacojayy, StevenMXZ). Thanks to **Yurim** for testing and approving it on real hardware. - **🖥️ Foldable Screen Alignment (#413)** — **requested by Igoryaos** (Honor Magic V2 foldable), who scoped out the handheld-split idea; implemented in Bannerlator. - **🎞️ Frame-generation flicker / FPS fix** — on the **[lsfg-vk](https://github.com/PancakeTAS/lsfg-vk)** (PancakeTAS · **GPL-3.0**) + **[lsfg-vk-android](https://github.com/FrankBarretta/lsfg-vk-android)** (FrankBarretta · MIT) engine behind the Lossless Scaling FG option. *No proprietary Lossless Scaling shaders are bundled — you supply your own `Lossless.dll` (from [Lossless Scaling](https://store.steampowered.com/app/993090/) by THS).* - **🛒 Steam large-download fix (#408)** — built on **[GameNative](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative)**'s (utkarshdalal · **GPL-3.0**) disk-spooling **[JavaSteam](https://github.com/Longi94/JavaSteam)** fork (Longi94 · MIT). - Everyone testing on real hardware and filing **Mali reports** with logs. ❤️ --- *Entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall. Install over 3.0.0; everything carries over.*

releases.name: Bannerlator 3.0.0
releases.body:
# Bannerlator 3.0.0 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **3.0.0 is the big stable release**, rolling up everything shipped since 2.9.9 — including the `3.0.0-pre1` and `3.0.0-pre2` opt-in betas. It's headlined by a brand-new **three-engine audio stack**, a huge push on the **GOG, Epic and Steam storefronts with automatic cloud saves**, and deeper **graphics, rendering and performance** controls. As always the update is **entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall** — so your containers, Wine installs, themes, accent colour and per-game settings all carry over untouched. Install straight over 2.9.9. # What's New — everything since 2.9.9 ## 🔊 New audio stack — the 3.0 headline Audio has been rebuilt from the ground up around a low-latency, self-healing engine, with real controls instead of a black box: - **New adaptive PulseAudio engine** — a freshly rebuilt sound path that automatically grows its buffer when it hears crackle/underruns and re-opens cleanly when your output changes (speaker → headphones → Bluetooth → HDMI), so audio recovers instead of dying. - **Audio settings you can actually use** — an Audio cog in the container editor, in each game's shortcut settings, and on the in-game side-menu, with presets, fine-tune rows, and a **"?" explanation on every preset and row** so you know what each one does. - **Latency slider that really works** — the slider now drives the engine's buffer directly, and greyed-out rows honestly show what your chosen preset is actually applying. - **Second engine: adaptive ALSA** — a full alternative audio path with its own presets and fine-tune mirror, for devices/games that prefer it. - **Third engine: DirectAudio (experimental)** — an optional lower-latency driver with live in-game tuning; PulseAudio remains the safe default, and DirectAudio is clearly labelled experimental. It's supported on the current arm64ec Proton builds and auto-updates itself when you're on one. - **No cross-engine bleed** — each engine and scope keeps its own settings, so changing one never silently rewrites another. - **Smoother background/foreground** — audio only re-initialises on a real output change, not every time you tab away. ## 🛒 Storefronts & cloud saves — GOG, Epic & Steam A massive storefront push brings GOG, Epic and Steam much closer to a native launcher — with automatic cloud saves across all three. **GOG (major overhaul):** - **Automatic cloud saves** — Bannerlator now finds each GOG game's save folder for you (no manual folder picking), **uploads your saves to GOG cloud when you exit** and **pulls the latest down when you launch**, just like Galaxy. Sync is parallel and fast, syncs subfolders, uses newest-wins so it never clobbers a newer save, and **skips files that haven't actually changed** (content-checked, not just timestamps) so unchanged saves never re-transfer. - **Reliable installs** — three-layer MD5 integrity checking, size+hash resume verification, a **Verify / Repair Files** button, automatic secure-link refresh on server hiccups, a **pre-flight free-space guard**, and CSRF protection on sign-in. - **Automatic prerequisites** — required Visual C++/runtime redistributables are downloaded and installed into the game's container for you when you add a GOG game. - **DLC installs** — per-DLC **Install** buttons that fetch and install each add-on into the base game (this also fixed a bug that stopped some DLC-bearing titles from installing at all). - **Faster downloads** — smarter, device-aware parallel downloading with largest-files-first scheduling. - **Nicer library** — a dedicated GOG tab in the Save Manager, GOG badges on your game cards and lists, tall poster cover art, and faster library refreshes. **Epic / Epic Online Services (EOS):** - **Epic cloud saves** — a first-class Epic tab in the Save Manager with automatic save-folder resolution and two-way sync, restoring your files to the right place. - **Proper Epic sign-in & launching** — real Epic launch-time authentication and EOS game identification, with **EPIC / EOS badges** on cover art and in lists. - **Denuvo & offline support** — an ownership-token path for Denuvo titles (with a manual override), a per-game **Launch offline** toggle, and language-selective installs. - **A far more robust downloader** — cancel any install cleanly at any stage, keep-or-delete prompts on cancel, atomic chunk writes so a resumed download can't reuse a corrupt piece, plus delta/verify/repair. - **Polish** — in-app folder picker for the save location, wider grid columns, and de-duplicated library entries (fixes a crash some Epic libraries hit). **Steam:** - **One-tap Lossless Scaling setup** — a **Detect from Steam store** button finds the Lossless Scaling `Lossless.dll` from an in-app Steam install and wires it into frame generation for you, and the download now always pulls the current version instead of a stale duplicate. - **Beta branches** — pick a game's beta/branch (including password-gated ones) right on its detail page. - **Non-game apps** — tools like Lossless Scaling now show up in your library, and the install-complete check no longer false-fails games that share/de-duplicate depots. ## 🎮 Games & shortcuts - **The internal-storage hang fix** — games that stall on their intro movie when installed on internal/SD storage now have two clean fixes: **add a game directly from a container's Drive C**, or **Copy game to Drive C** (a one-tap helper that moves a game onto the container's fast C: drive and re-points the shortcut for you). Both leave your shortcut untouched if anything goes wrong. - **Change executable** — re-point any shortcut to a different `.exe` without recreating it. - **File picker that isn't stuck in Downloads** — the in-app file picker now opens at your storage root, and Back/Up work from any folder (applies everywhere you pick a file: drives, components, wallpaper, backups, imports). - **Responsive shortcut settings** — the per-game settings dialog now uses top tabs in portrait and a side rail in landscape, with a tidied title bar and a properly pinned OK/Cancel footer. - **Per-DLL toggles** — flip individual DLLs detected in a game's folder on or off (and a fix so turning one off actually sticks). - **Per-game graphics quick-settings persist** across relaunch (#382). - **Big Picture games wall (opt-in)** — a new landscape, couch-friendly library home; enable it in settings. The library header also doubles as your account entry point, and the Tools/Power/Game-options sheets now scroll properly. - **Unified install popup** — installs now show a single persistent progress popup with up-front details, a real **Cancel**, and live notifications. ## 🖥️ Graphics, rendering & performance - **Wrapper + Adreno Vulkan fix (#403)** — fixes DXVK/games refusing to start on **wrapper graphics drivers**, especially lower-tier Adreno (e.g. Adreno 610), with *"Device does not support Vulkan 1.3"* or *"Skipping Vulkan 1.0 adapter."* A clamp added back in 2.9.1 was reading the *system* driver's Vulkan version instead of the Turnip the guest actually wraps, dragging the reported version below DXVK's minimum; 3.0.0 restores the correct 2.8.1 behavior (and lowers the fresh-container default back to 1.3). Device-verified on Adreno 610; the final Vulkan version + probe result are now logged for easier troubleshooting. - **Hardened Native Rendering** — the Native renderer now runs through a more robust display path, with a per-container **and** per-game **backend picker** (Auto / SurfaceFlinger / Vulkan direct-scanout) plus a compositor-driver choice for full parity with the Vulkan settings. - **Frame generation, rebuilt clean-room (experimental)** — the old frame-gen layer has been fully removed and replaced with **win-fg**, a clean-room engine (built on AMD's open FidelityFX FSR3), with a simple Off/On toggle and model options in the in-game menu. Still experimental while we tune quality. - **Samsung Galaxy performance control (no root)** — on supported Galaxy devices, an opt-in power-control path for CPU/GPU/RAM with per-game presets and a recommendation to avoid it fighting the root power tier. Bannerlator also now signals active gameplay to Android's game mode across vendors. - **Performance dashboard** — a live performance dialog reachable both in-game and from per-game settings. - **Fusion HUD** — a battery-temperature (**BAT °C**) chip on the pill, a much more accurate graphics-API label (correctly tells DXVK from VKD3D, even for dual-API apps), and the HUD now goes fully idle when you turn it off (no wasted per-frame work). Toggling **Show HUD** on in-game also turns the FPS counter on and builds the overlay live — no relaunch. - **Contents hub (new)** — a single place to browse, install and remove GPU drivers and components (DXVK/VKD3D/D8VK/D7VK and more), with opt-in community sources, an **Installed** tab to remove things, and an in-app file picker for local files. - **Driver stability** — fixed a hard crash when selecting custom Adreno drivers on some chips, and custom/Turnip drivers now show a reassuring note instead of a misleading "0 extensions" error. - **Interface Scale** — new UI + font size sliders (with −/+ steppers); the interface defaults to a slightly more compact 90%. - **Advanced** — an opt-in guest-memory cap (`WINEVMEMMAXSIZE`) for titles that need it, and the in-app updater now cleans up stale downloaded APKs. ## 🐛 Stability & fixes - **Crash reports without root** — native crashes are now captured (and decoded into a real backtrace) even on non-rooted devices. - **Backgrounding & pausing** — games with very long executable names now pause correctly when backgrounded. - **Launch robustness** — a single malformed environment variable is skipped (and named while you type) instead of aborting the launch. - **X server** — assorted memory-leak and crash fixes (DRI3 pixmap leak, a malformed atom-name reply, and a config-parsing bug that dropped single-item settings). - Plus a wide sweep of UI polish and readability fixes (e.g. save-sync and install status now use a readable themed bar instead of unreadable pop-ups on some ROMs). ## ⚠️ Notes & known limitations - **Controllers are unchanged from 2.9.9.** All the new controller work (per-controller profile assignment and the input slot-takeover rework) is **parked** — it needs more time to get right, and I didn't want it holding up 3.0. Controller behaviour is exactly as it was in 2.9.9; nothing there has changed. It'll return in a later build once it's properly tested. - **The Big Picture games wall is still a little rough.** The opt-in landscape games wall is usable but has some edges to iron out — expect a few rough spots while it's polished in a follow-up. - **Proton layers are already included.** Every current released Proton layer is available in-app — install or update them from the **Contents** hub or the **in-game catalog downloads**. There's no separate Proton download to grab for this release (the Proton 9 link below is optional/legacy). --- ## 📦 Where to get Proton 9 The APK does not bundle any Wine — Wine installs from the in-app catalog. > ⚠️ **A fresh install ships with no Wine at all.** On first run, open **Containers → the download icon** and install a Proton before creating a container. Updating from 2.9.9 changes nothing — your existing containers and Wine installs are untouched. **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** — not bundled, download it if you want it: **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-arm64ec.wcp** 66.7 MB · sha256 `f8a99fed387f1b097009129dc49368c8f500927640a9d4c7a192d850b1b2068c` Install it via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. It also appears in the in-app catalog. *(Compiled as a wcp by **Xnick417x**.)*

 

## 🙏 Credits & licenses Bannerlator is distributed under **GPL-3.0** because it incorporates GPL-licensed components (below). The complete, authoritative attribution list — including the **MIT Winlator lineage (© 2023 BrunoSX)** this app descends from and every shader/library license — lives in **[THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/blob/main/THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md)**. Highlights for this release: - **[GameNative](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative)** (utkarshdalal · **GPL-3.0**) — incorporated for the Proton bionic translation, the `AHardwareBuffer` present/scanout path that the hardened Native Rendering builds on, the standalone FPS limiter (present-pacing throttle), and the Steam session-hardening + download-speed model. Its storefront/cloud-save feature set was also the parity target that guided this cycle's GOG and Epic work. Bannerlator is GPL-3.0 as a result — with thanks. - **[lsfg-vk](https://github.com/PancakeTAS/lsfg-vk)** (PancakeTAS · **GPL-3.0**) + **[lsfg-vk-android](https://github.com/FrankBarretta/lsfg-vk-android)** (FrankBarretta · MIT) — the Vulkan frame-generation engine behind the Lossless Scaling FG option that this release's one-tap **Detect from Steam store** feature wires up. *No proprietary Lossless Scaling shaders are bundled — you supply your own `Lossless.dll` (from [Lossless Scaling](https://store.steampowered.com/app/993090/) by THS).* - **win-fg** — Bannerlator's own **clean-room** default frame-gen engine; its optical-flow front end adapts **AMD FidelityFX FSR3** (MIT), with synthesis written from first principles and **no proprietary code or weights**. (This is separate from the GPL frame-gen path above — win-fg ships no GPL frame-gen code.) - **Samsung Galaxy Performance SDK** (Samsung Electronics · proprietary) — powers the optional no-root Galaxy CPU/GPU/RAM control. The SDK is **not** redistributed in this repo; the feature stays dormant without it. - **PulseAudio & ALSA** (LGPL) — the foundations the new adaptive audio engines are built on, and **[DirectAudio](https://github.com/The412Banner/directaudio)** (LGPL-2.1) — the experimental third audio engine. - **[JavaSteam](https://github.com/Longi94/JavaSteam)** (Longi94 · MIT) + `javasteam-depotdownloader` (joshuatam) — the Steam connection + depot-download engine behind the Steam-store improvements. - **[VEGAS DXVK](https://github.com/isygold/vegas-releases)** (isygold) — the Adreno-tuned DXVK builds so much of our performance rides on. - **Xnick417x** — the working **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** `.wcp` linked above. - **WinNative** — the controller input-ring hardening ported in this cycle. - The **Winlator / Star** lineage (**MIT © 2023 BrunoSX** — brunodev85, coffincolors, Pipetto-crypto, jacojayy, StevenMXZ) this project is built on. - Everyone filing **Mali reports** with logs, testing build after build, and adding games and configs to **BannerHub & Bannerlator**. ❤️ --- *Entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall. Install over 2.9.9; everything carries over.*

releases.name: Bannerlator 3.0.0 — Pre-Release 2
releases.body: # Bannerlator 3.0.0 — Pre-Release 2 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. > 🧪 **This is an opt-in beta, not a stable release.** You're only seeing it because you turned on **Settings → Include pre-releases**. Stable users stay on **2.9.9** and won't be offered this. It installs **entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall** — so your containers, themes, accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. > 🧱 **Builds on Pre-Release 1.** Everything from 3.0.0-pre1 is here — the ground-up **audio stack** (DirectAudio + adaptive PulseAudio/ALSA), the **Contents hub**, and the Adreno a6xx driver-crash fix. This cut is about what landed **since** pre1: a full **Epic Games Store / EOS** experience, a unified **install-progress** UI, an in-game **graphics-API label** fix, a **controller input-death** fix, and heavy-game **memory** headroom. --- # What's New — since Pre-Release 1 ## 🎮 Epic Games Store — real EOS support (the headline) Bannerlator's Epic support graduated from "launches games" to a genuine, badged, cancel-safe store experience with **Epic Online Services (EOS)** identity and authentication. - **Real launch-arg authentication + EOS identification** — the launcher injects the genuine Epic launch arguments (auth, exchange, locale) so EOS titles that demand a valid session actually start, and the app identifies which of your games are EOS-backed. - **EPIC / EOS badges everywhere** — a store **EPIC** badge and an **EOS** badge overlay the cover art (top-left) in grid views and sit beside the game name in list rows, with an **EOS chip on the launch splash** so you know what's starting. Grid columns were widened to fit. - **Denuvo-aware ownership token** — for EOS titles behind Denuvo, an ownership token (`-epicovt`) is passed when needed, gated by a Denuvo heuristic (literal-string scan + shipping-exe size) with a **per-shortcut "Force Denuvo ownership token"** override for edge cases. - **Per-shortcut "Launch offline"** — a toggle to launch an Epic title without the online auth handshake, with the Denuvo/Offline sub-toggles sensibly greyed out when EOS auth isn't in play. - **Selective install tags** — pick which optional content (e.g. **language** packs) to install, plus **delta / verify / repair** so you only pull what changed. - **A cancel-safe, resume-safe downloader** — this was a large reliability pass: - Cancel is now honored across **every** phase — the chunk pool, the delta-verify phase, and the manifest/CDN phase — so pressing cancel actually stops the whole job. - A **keep-or-delete dialog** on cancel, synced across all three surfaces (library, detail, in-progress), so the action buttons always reflect the real state; delete-on-cancel also clears the install record so no stale "Resume/Play" buttons linger. - **Atomic chunk writes** — a chunk is written to a temp file and swapped into place, so an interrupted download can never leave a **truncated chunk** that a later resume would silently reuse (a class of corrupted-install bug). - **Launch quick-wins** — locale/offline arguments, ownership-token and AdditionalCommandLine caching, and per-game fixes; plus a library **de-duplication** pass so a game can't appear twice. ## 📦 Contents — a unified install experience The Contents hub (new in pre1) got the install flow it deserved, and the same popup now drives container-side component installs too. - **One shared install popup** — a live progress dialog used by **both** the Contents hub and the New/Edit-container component installer, so installing looks and behaves identically wherever you start it. - **Live two-pass progress bar** — download fills in a darker accent, install sweeps a lighter accent over it, finishing matched to your theme accent (no stray colours). Local-file installs show a single install bar (there's nothing to download). - **Metadata up front** — the component **type, description and version** are read from the package and shown from the first frame, instead of only appearing at the end. - **A real Cancel** — cancelling actually stops the install (best-effort on a native extract), and the finished popup **stays open until you close it** so you can read what happened. Progress also shows as a **live percentage in the Android notification shade**. - **Save location, de-duplicated** — the "Save location" control now lives in one place (the Contents settings cog) instead of being shown twice. - **A D7VK browse chip** in the Nightlies source, and a fix for a **crash when deleting a component** from the Installed tab. ## 🖥️ In-game HUD — accurate graphics-API label The Fusion HUD's API label (DXVK / VKD3D / D3D12 …) was wrong for many modern games on **arm64ec** — a D3D12/VKD3D title (e.g. *GTA V Enhanced*) could read **DXVK**. - **Root cause:** on arm64ec the DirectX modules aren't visible the old way (they're not mapped where the HUD looked), so the label fell back to the container's configured wrapper name. - **The fix:** a layered resolver that reads the game's **own** ground-truth signals in priority order — an app self-report, the game engine's log (Unity `Player.log`), then the wrapper's own logs (VKD3D / DXVK) — before falling back. It works even with the log toggle off (a tiny private log is written just for the label), and it now labels **dual-API games correctly**: a title that offers both DX11 and DX12 (e.g. *Deus Ex: Mankind Divided*) reads **D3D11** in DX11 mode and **D3D12** in DX12 mode, instead of being fooled by a startup D3D12 capability probe. - **HUD polish** — the in-game **Show HUD** toggle now turns the FPS counter on and builds the overlay live, and the HUD's background threads idle while it's off (a small battery/CPU win). ## 🎮 Controllers — input-death-mid-game fix A frustrating bug where **controller input could stop reaching the game mid-session** is fixed (ported from WinNative #603): - The fake-input ring buffer capacity was raised **512 → 4096**, with proper **store-release fences** around its seqlock publishes, closing a race that could wedge the input pipe. - Controllers are **neutralised when the in-game drawer opens**, so opening the overlay can't leave a stuck input. > Note: this is the **input-death** fix. The larger controller **slot-takeover / player-assignment overhaul** (#345) is still being finished and is **not** in this build. ## 🍷 Heavy-game memory headroom — WINEVMEMMAXSIZE Some very large titles reserve an enormous virtual-address space up front (e.g. *Deus Ex: Mankind Divided*'s ~489 GB reservation) and fail on the guest. - A new **`WINEVMEMMAXSIZE`** knob lets you **cap the guest Wine VA reservation**. It's **opt-in and default-off** (nothing changes unless you set it) and is recognised in the env-var picker. ## 🎞️ Frame generation — win-fg bring-up progress win-fg (the clean-room replacement introduced in pre1) advanced toward working frame generation: - **Phase 3a** interpolated-frame **synthesis + blit** is now bundled, with automatic background/foreground reset pulses on toggle-on and model change so the layer re-initialises cleanly, and the bundled runtime `.so` was refreshed several times (swapchain+1, HUD-rect masking, quality tuning). > ⚠️ **Still experimental.** Frame *insertion* bring-up is ongoing; treat win-fg as a work-in-progress. If you want working frame generation today, **lsfg-vk** remains available and unaffected. --- ## ⚠️ Known limitations in this build - **win-fg** frame generation is still in bring-up (see above). - The controller **slot-takeover overhaul (#345)** is **not** merged yet — only the input-death fix above is included. - The HUD probe-gate for dual-API games is fresh; if you see a mislabel on an unusual title, that's a bug report we want. - Epic **Denuvo** ownership-token support is best-effort and hard to verify (few runnable Denuvo-on-EOS titles exist); it's inert unless a game needs it. ## ➕ Everything from Pre-Release 1 and 2.9.9, carried forward All of pre1 (the audio stack, Contents hub, a6xx driver-crash fix, X-server correctness fixes, interface-scale sliders) and all of 2.9.9 are included unchanged underneath this. --- ## 🙏 Credits — for the work in this build The changes since Pre-Release 1 build directly on: - **WinNative** — the controller input-ring hardening (#603) adapted here for the input-death-mid-game fix (GPL-3.0). - **GameNative** — the Epic Games Store / EOS plumbing and download model referenced for parity. - **[VKD3D-Proton](https://github.com/HansKristian-Work/vkd3d-proton)** and **[DXVK](https://github.com/doitsujin/dxvk)** — the Direct3D → Vulkan wrappers whose own logs power the new, accurate in-game API label (and which run the games it labels). - **AMD FidelityFX FSR3** (MIT) — the optical-flow front-end behind win-fg's frame-generation bring-up. - **Wine / Proton** and **[GE-Proton](https://github.com/GloriousEggroll/proton-ge-custom)** (GloriousEggroll) — the runtime the new `WINEVMEMMAXSIZE` guest-memory cap builds on. And thank you to everyone on the **pre-release channel** who tested builds and filed reports this cycle — the HUD-label and Epic download fixes came straight out of that. _(The full upstream credits for everything Bannerlator is built on — Winlator, Wine/Proton, FEX, Box64, Mesa/Turnip, DXVK/VKD3D, DirectAudio and more — are carried in the repo and earlier releases.)_ --- ### 📖 Also available as a standalone document The same breakdown lives in the repo for easy linking/reading: **→ [Bannerlator 3.0.0-pre2 — Detailed Changelog](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/blob/3.0.0-pre2/docs/releases/3.0.0-pre2.md)** _Report anything you hit — that's what a pre-release is for._

releases.name: Bannerlator 3.0.0 — Pre-Release 1
releases.body: # Bannerlator 3.0.0 — Pre-Release 1 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. > 🧪 **This is an opt-in beta, not a stable release.** You're only seeing it because you turned on **Settings → Include pre-releases**. Its purpose is to get the new **DirectAudio** engine and the **adaptive PulseAudio / ALSA** stacks into testers' hands early. Stable users stay on 2.9.9 and won't be offered this. It installs **entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall** — so your containers, themes, accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. > 🎮 **Controllers are unchanged from 2.9.9.** The reworked controller-input / player-slot system is **not** in this build — controller behaviour is identical to 2.9.9. This cut is scoped to audio. The controller overhaul lands in a later 3.0 build. --- # What's New — everything since 2.9.9 ## 🔊 A ground-up audio stack (3.0's headline) 2.9.9 promised a "ground-up audio stack" for 3.0. This is it. Three engines, all made adaptive, all controllable live, with a strict configuration model so settings never leak across engines or scopes. ### Adaptive PulseAudio 13 sink The PulseAudio path (the default engine) was rebuilt from stock PulseAudio 13 in CI with a re-derived AAudio sink module: - **Adaptive buffering** — the sink grows its buffer on underrun (xrun) instead of crackling, then holds the smaller latency when the stream is stable. - **Route-change recreate, foreground *and* background** — plug/unplug wired, USB-C, Bluetooth or HDMI and the sink is recreated cleanly onto the new device; route changes made while the app is backgrounded are recovered on return to foreground. - **Background/foreground smoothing** — the sink only recreates on a *real* route change, not on every focus flip, so pausing and resuming no longer pops the audio. - **Mute-bug fix** — the module is now handed `volume=1.0` so an absent-volume default can't leave the sink silent. ### Adaptive ALSA driver The ALSA engine got the same adaptive treatment: - **Grow-on-underrun + reopen-on-route-change**, mirroring the PulseAudio behaviour. - **`PERFORMANCE_MODE_NONE` fix** — the ALSA path no longer requests a performance mode it never actually read, and its buffer bookkeeping is now honest. - **Full settings mirror** — the ALSA engine exposes the same presets and fine-tune rows as the others. ### DirectAudio — a new third audio engine (experimental, opt-in) A brand-new first-class audio engine sits alongside PulseAudio and ALSA. Under the hood it's a **native Wine → Android AAudio driver** (`winedirectaudio.drv`) that hands the game's audio **straight to Android's low-level AAudio API — with no PulseAudio or ALSA middleman** in between. That shorter path is the whole point: fewer hops is headroom for **lower latency and cleaner output**. It's a young, purpose-built, open project with real room to grow — the long-term aim is for it to become the **lowest-latency, best-sounding of the three engines**, surpassing the PulseAudio and ALSA paths as it matures. It's **experimental today**, which is exactly why it's landing in a pre-release first. > 📦 **Open source (LGPL-2.1):** [github.com/The412Banner/directaudio](https://github.com/The412Banner/directaudio) — the standalone driver, consumed here as a submodule. Read the source, follow its progress, or contribute. The engine itself: - **Opt-in and clearly labelled experimental** — the default stays PulseAudio; DirectAudio is a choice, with a warning on the selector. - **Bundles driver v1.3.1**, overlaid into the Proton layer at launch. - **⚠️ DirectAudio only works with the four rebuilt arm64ec compatibility layers** — **Proton 10.0-4, 11.0-1, 11.0-3, and 11.0-5** (arm64ec). Its `winedirectaudio.drv` is built against exactly those builds; on any other layer the option is greyed out and the launch falls back to the default driver. You download these layers **in-app through Contents** (published in the `contents.json` catalog), and the bundled driver auto-updates into whichever one you're on. - **Live in-game control** — the in-game audio cog applies DirectAudio changes through the driver mailbox without a relaunch. - **Sensible presets** — real preset buffers, the 33 ms default the driver already ships, a safety-net Low preset on every engine, and `POWER_SAVING` is deliberately *not* offered for DirectAudio because it churns under FEX. ### Audio controls, everywhere (the cog) Audio is now tunable from every scope that matters, with the same UI: - **Container editor cog** and a **per-game shortcut cog** (Compose `ShortcutSettingsDialogScreen`), plus a dedicated **in-game Audio tab**. - **Presets + fine-tune rows** with **per-preset and per-row "?" help**, and greyed rows now *show* what the selected preset actually applies rather than looking broken. - The cog's **latency slider actually sets the buffer** now (it was previously inert for DirectAudio). - The in-game cog **no longer deletes hand-set driver knobs**, and the DirectAudio knobs are available in the add-variable catalog. ### Strict per-scope / per-engine configuration (no bleed) Under the hood the audio settings were re-architected so configuration can't leak across axes: - **Independent per-engine preference stores** — PulseAudio, ALSA and DirectAudio each keep their own settings; switching engines no longer inherits stale values from another. - **Per-scope hierarchy** — persistent (per-container, engine-scoped env keys), runtime (ephemeral `banner_audio_`), and in-game (shortcut-only) are kept separate with a full baseline seed at launch, so nothing bleeds between container / shortcut / in-game. - **Malformed env variables** are skipped (with an explanation while you type) instead of crashing the launch. ## 🎞️ Frame generation: bionic-fg → clean-room win-fg The previous frame-generation layer (bionic-fg) was **removed** because its LSFG weights were proprietary.
