It is replaced by **win-fg**, a clean-room implementation built to honour that takedown: - **All tainted models are gone** from the app, READMEs and license/third-party notices; win-fg and its FidelityFX FSR3 (MIT) optical-flow front-end are recorded instead. - **New in-game controls** — frame generation is now **Off / On (On = 2×)**; turning it On reveals the model choice (**Optical flow / Bidirectional**) and a flow-scale control. The old bionic-fg model toggles, spec cards, launch splash and in-game drawer badge are all replaced with win-fg's. - **Device-proven runtime .so bundled** (present-fix + hot-reload + always-init). > ⚠️ **Known limitation this build:** win-fg is still in on-device **bring-up**. Its frame-*insertion* stage isn't finished, so **frame generation currently runs as passthrough** — the pipeline is wired end-to-end and the UI is live, but generated frames aren't inserted yet. This is exactly why 3.0.0-pre1 is a pre-release. If you want working frame generation today, **lsfg-vk** remains available and unaffected. ## 📦 The new Contents hub A new **Contents** manager replaces the scattered add/install entry points with one multi-source hub for drivers, components, wrappers and raw archives: - **Hub screen with tabs and master-detail** — badges, a "My Files" area, and an **Installed** tab to view and remove drivers and components you've added. - **Multi-source remote engine** — a type registry and raw-archive library pulling from multiple sources, with **token-based cross-source search** and a clear-search button. - **Community repos are opt-in**, per-source toggles with grouped provenance so you see where each item comes from; the old default source was dropped. - **In-app file picker** on the install buttons, and search results shown in the right pane in landscape. - **Process-lifetime installer** — the `.wcp` pipeline, adrenotools drivers and a keep-raw option run for the life of the install. - **Layout & polish** — a left `NavigationRail` for tabs in landscape / top `TabRow` in portrait, `VerticalDivider` fix for the empty detail pane, scroll-clipping fixes at large UI scale, de-duplicated titles/keys (fixing a duplicate-key crash) and ghost white-button fixes. - Adrenotools is **hidden from the drawer** and folded into the Contents entry in its System slot. ## 🖥️ Turnip / driver-select stability (the Adreno a6xx crash fix) A hard crash when selecting custom adrenotools drivers on **Adreno a6xx** devices is fixed: - **Proprietary Qualcomm driver blobs are no longer probed in-app** — probing them in-process could smash the stack (`SIGABRT`) or corrupt the linker heap. Custom drivers still load and work at game launch; they simply show a **reassuring note** in the picker instead of being probed. - **Turnip / Mesa drivers still list their extensions** as before; only the proprietary blobs are skipped. - **The probe was moved off the main thread** (killing an ANR), serialised behind a mutex, with a **`SIGABRT` guard** as a backstop. - A true **0 / 0** result now shows the reassuring in-game note, never a misleading "0 extensions" error. ## 🩹 X-server correctness & leak fixes Several portable correctness fixes in the pure-Java X server: - **DRI3 pixmaps are now registered as client resources**, stopping a resource leak. - **`GetAtomName`** malformed-reply and out-of-range-atom crash fixed. - **`KeyValueSet`** iterator no longer drops single-item configs. - **Long-exe-name games** are now correctly suspended on pause (matching the full cmdline, not the truncated `comm`). > A separate Present/Sync per-window resource-prune leak fix was trialled and **reverted** — on-device it forced a CPU pacer that tanked framerates — so it is intentionally **not** in this build. There is no framerate regression here. ## ✨ Appearance & HUD - **Interface Scale** — new UI + font-size sliders (with −/+ steppers) in Appearance, defaulting to **90%**. Verified not to affect the on-screen controls, HUD, or the game surface itself. - **HUD battery temperature** — the Fusion HUD pill now shows a **"BAT °C"** chip next to the RAM chip. ## 🔧 Updater, diagnostics & misc - **Update-cache pruning** — the in-app updater now prunes stale downloaded APKs before each download *and* on cold start, fixing an accumulation that could reach ~10 GB over many versions. - **No-root native-crash capture** — native crashes are captured via `ApplicationExitInfo` even without root, and the crash tombstone proto is decoded into a real backtrace for bug reports. ## 🚫 What this build does *not* include (yet) To be explicit, because it's a common question: - **The reworked controller-input / player-slot system is NOT in this build.** Controller behaviour here is **exactly the same as 2.9.9** — the same hot-plug, slot and on-screen-controls handling. The newer controller work (slot-takeover / player-assignment overhaul) is still being finished and verified and has not been merged; it will come in a later 3.0 build. Updating to 3.0.0-pre1 does **not** change how your controllers behave versus 2.9.9. This pre-release is intentionally scoped to the **audio stack** (DirectAudio + adaptive PulseAudio/ALSA) plus the driver-crash fix, Contents hub and the polish items above — nothing about controllers changed. ## ➕ Everything from 2.9.9, carried forward All of 2.9.9 is included — including its controller/touch input fixes and deeper log capture, unchanged — on top of the 2.9.8 headphone-following audio and 2.9.7 controller reliability overhaul. --- ### 📖 Also available as a standalone document The same breakdown lives in the repo for easy linking/reading: **→ [Bannerlator 3.0.0-pre1 — Detailed Changelog](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/blob/3.0.0-pre1/docs/releases/3.0.0-pre1.md)** _Report anything you hit — that's what a pre-release is for._

releases.name: Bannerlator 2.9.9
releases.body:
# Bannerlator 2.9.9 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **2.9.9 is a hotfix over 2.9.8.** It turns the still-in-progress TV / external-display feature *off* for now, folds in a controller-input fix, and makes the log capture more useful for bug reports. As always it's **entirely app-side** — **no ImageFS reinstall** — your containers, themes, custom accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. Install straight over 2.9.8. > 🙏 **Sorry for the churn.** 2.9.8 shipped the TV / external-display feature before it was really ready — it broke on **Samsung DeX and Motorola** desktop modes (games wouldn't go fullscreen, the HUD vanished, the mouse died), and a couple of other rough edges slipped through. That's on me. This quick **2.9.9** turnaround is to put things right by pulling that feature until it's actually finished, rather than leaving a half-working release up. Thanks for the reports and for your patience. ## 📺 TV / external-display output — temporarily turned off After reports that it misbehaved on **Samsung (DeX) and Motorola devices** ([#339](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/issues/339)) — the game would try to go fullscreen and fail, the FPS HUD would vanish, and the mouse would stop working — the whole **TV output feature is disabled in 2.9.9** while it's finished and properly tested: - **Plugging in a TV (or entering DeX) no longer pushes the game to the external display.** The game stays on your handheld, with the HUD and pointer working normally. - The in-game **TV tab is hidden**, and the experimental wireless casting picker is off with it. - **Nothing is lost** — this is a clean on/off switch. Your saved TV settings stay on disk, and the whole feature (with the DeX fix in place) will return in a future build once it's solid. > If you were relying on wired external-display output, sit tight — it's coming back, fixed. This release removes it rather than shipping it half-working. ## 🎮 Controller & touch input fix - An explicit **"-- Disabled --"** touch-controls choice is now honored and stays disabled across launches — no more phantom on-screen pad reappearing, and no fake touchscreen timeout. Fixes [#338](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/issues/338) (thanks **@NaufalFajri**). - When a **physical controller is already connected at launch**, the smart-default on-screen pad no longer spawns — it was grabbing a player slot and fighting your real controller. ## 📝 Deeper log capture for bug reports **Log Manager → "Capture logcat now"** now grabs up to **10,000 lines** of the app's own log (was 1,000), so a captured log reaches much further back when something goes wrong. It's still **app-scoped and redacted** — safe to share — and captured on demand, never streamed, so it doesn't slow a game down. ## ➕ Everything from 2.9.8, carried forward All of 2.9.8 is included — the **audio that follows your headphones** (plug/unplug wired · USB-C · Bluetooth · HDMI mid-game and the sound moves within about half a second, both directions) and **audio recovery on background/foreground** — on top of everything from 2.9.7 (the controller reliability overhaul, two-tier Free Memory, Task Manager Processor Affinity readback) and 2.9.6. ## 🔊 Coming soon in 3.0 — a ground-up audio stack Not in this build, but in the works for **3.0**: the guest audio path has been **rebuilt from the ground up** on **PulseAudio 13.0** (cross-compiled from source) with a brand-new **adaptive AAudio sink** that **smart-adjusts on the fly** to keep sound smooth. It comes with real audio controls, too — a dedicated in-game **Audio tab** and a container-editor **Audio** panel with **presets + fine-tuning** and **guest-latency** control, applied live. Still cooking and being proven on-device — landing in a future release. ## 📦 Where to get Proton 9 The APK does not bundle Proton 9 — Wine installs from the in-app catalog on first run. > ⚠️ **A fresh install ships with no Wine at all.** On first run, open **Containers → the download icon** and install a Proton before creating a container. Updating from 2.9.8 changes nothing — your existing containers and Wine installs are untouched. **Proton 9.0 — not bundled; grab whichever matches your setup (both also appear in the in-app catalog):** **arm64ec** (default for most devices): **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-arm64ec.wcp** 66.7 MB · sha256 `f8a99fed387f1b097009129dc49368c8f500927640a9d4c7a192d850b1b2068c` **x86_64**: **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-x86_64.wcp** 50.7 MB · sha256 `ec90286b2b266aaa9dd4c5265383a48f05ccc96890d078cb3529e78b89cba2ea` Install via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. *(Compiled as wcps by **Xnick417x**.)*

 

## 🙏 Credits - **@NaufalFajri** — [#338](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/issues/338), the touch-controls / timeout report. - **@degortg-cell** — [#339](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/issues/339), the Samsung DeX / Motorola desktop-mode report that prompted turning TV output off until it's finished. - **isygold** — **[Vegas DXVK](https://github.com/isygold/vegas-releases)**, the community DXVK builds so much of our performance rides on. - **Xnick417x** — the Proton 9.0 arm64ec + x86_64 `.wcp`s linked above. - And everyone reporting, testing build after build, and adding games and configs to BannerHub & Bannerlator. ❤️ --- > ℹ️ **Root is only needed for the root-gated performance tier** (governor / CPU-clock / thermal / fan) and the **Deep clean** memory tier. Everything else — including **non-root GPU max-clock** on Adreno — needs no root. The root tier stays opt-in, gated behind an explicit "use at your own risk" agreement, and every change auto-reverts when you leave the game. *Entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall. Install over 2.9.8; everything carries over.*

releases.name: Bannerlator 2.9.8
releases.body:
# Bannerlator 2.9.8 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **2.9.8 continues the road to 3.0** with a focus on **audio** and **playing on the big screen** — plus a batch of stability fixes. Everything from 2.9.7 is included. As always it's **entirely app-side** — **no ImageFS reinstall** — your containers, themes, custom accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. Install straight over 2.9.7. ## 🎧 Audio that follows your headphones The headline of 2.9.8 — game audio now goes where your ears are. - **Plug or unplug headphones mid-game and the sound follows.** Previously, plugging in wired headphones during a game did nothing (audio stayed on the speaker or went silent), and unplugging could leave the game muted — headphones only worked if they were already in *before* you launched. Now the moment you plug in or pull out **wired, USB-C, Bluetooth, or HDMI** audio, the game's sound moves to the new output within about half a second, in both directions. - **Under the hood:** an output-route change tears down the guest's audio stream, and a torn-down stream can't simply be "resumed." Bannerlator now rebuilds the audio path onto the new device on the fly and slides the game's sound over onto it — without restarting audio or interrupting the game. - **Audio recovery on background/foreground and TV** — coming back to a game (or switching to an HDMI TV) no longer leaves it silent; the audio output is re-established automatically on return. There's also a **"Reset audio"** button in the TV options if you ever need to nudge it manually. ## 📺 Play on your TV — new TV Options Send a game to an external display (USB-C → HDMI or a dock) and use the handheld as the controller, with a dedicated **TV** options panel: - **Aspect ratio, scaling, and render resolution** for the TV output, **overscan** correction (kills the black bars some TVs add), **latency** and **frame-cap / frame-gen** controls, an **audio-route** selector, and **dim-handheld** (dims the phone screen to save battery and heat while you play on the TV). - A **pause pill** shows on the TV and an **on-phone badge** makes it clear where the game is running. > 💡 **For the best TV experience, use a wired connection** (USB-C → HDMI / dock) — it's low-latency and carries full audio. ## 📡 Wireless casting — ⚠️ experimental, video-only New **no-app wireless casting**: stream a game to a **Chromecast / Google TV** straight from the in-app Cast picker — **nothing to install on the TV**. This is an early, experimental feature: there's noticeable latency and **game audio stays on the phone for now** (TV audio over cast is a work in progress). Treat it as a fun extra — for real play on a TV, use the **wired** external-display path above. ## 🔕 Quieter session notification The "session running" notification no longer pops up and makes a sound on every container/game launch — it now sits **silently** in the notification shade. The background-keepalive service is unchanged, so backgrounded games still stay alive. ## 🎮 Controller polish Building on 2.9.7's controller overhaul: - **On-screen controls auto-hide** when a physical controller is connected, and come back when it disconnects. - **Copy bindings** between controllers, and the **External Controllers** / **Players** lists now refresh live on hot-plug so what you see always matches what's connected. ## 🩹 Stability fixes - **Renderer / X-server bug fixes** — a batch of correctness fixes in the display path. - **Cleaner exit** — swiping the app away now reliably tears down stale Wine processes so the next launch starts clean. - **CPU affinity holds** — a host-side re-pin keeps your chosen processor affinity from drifting back onto disabled cores during play. ## ➕ Everything from 2.9.7, carried forward All of 2.9.7 is included — the **controller reliability overhaul** (hot-plug player slots, on-screen-input fix, capability filter, Players panel, status toast, Reset Input), the **two-tier Free Memory**, and the **Task Manager Processor Affinity** readback fix — on top of everything from 2.9.6 (portrait container-editor tabs, foreground-service keepalive, Turnip GMEM / TU_DEBUG tuning, cross-vendor performance HUD, "?" help + glossary everywhere, bundled AIO Graphics Test / Banner File Manager / Pale Moon, D7VK, IPv4 DNS fix). ## 📦 Where to get Proton 9 The APK does not bundle Proton 9 — Wine installs from the in-app catalog on first run. > ⚠️ **A fresh install ships with no Wine at all.** On first run, open **Containers → the download icon** and install a Proton before creating a container. Updating from 2.9.7 changes nothing — your existing containers and Wine installs are untouched. **Proton 9.0 — not bundled; grab whichever matches your setup (both also appear in the in-app catalog):** **arm64ec** (default for most devices): **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-arm64ec.wcp** 66.7 MB · sha256 `f8a99fed387f1b097009129dc49368c8f500927640a9d4c7a192d850b1b2068c` **x86_64**: **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-x86_64.wcp** 50.7 MB · sha256 `ec90286b2b266aaa9dd4c5265383a48f05ccc96890d078cb3529e78b89cba2ea` Install via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. *(Compiled as wcps by **Xnick417x**.)*

 

## 🙏 Credits - **Play-on-TV (external display) + audio recovery** — the external-display concept and the suspend-sink audio-recovery approach are credited to **[GameNative](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative)** (utkarshdalal). Our implementations are clean-room and original (the TV Options suite and the native audio client are our own), and the **wireless casting** feature is entirely original to Bannerlator. - **isygold** — **[Vegas DXVK](https://github.com/isygold/vegas-releases)**, the community DXVK builds so much of our performance rides on. - **Xnick417x** — the Proton 9.0 arm64ec + x86_64 `.wcp`s linked above. - Everyone filing **Mali reports** and issues with logs attached — the cross-vendor HUD and Mali paths keep getting proven on real hardware. - And everyone reporting, testing build after build, and adding games and configs to BannerHub & Bannerlator. ❤️ --- > ℹ️ **Root is only needed for the root-gated performance tier** (governor / CPU-clock / thermal / fan) and the **Deep clean** memory tier. Everything else — including **non-root GPU max-clock** on Adreno — needs no root. The root tier stays opt-in, gated behind an explicit "use at your own risk" agreement, and every change auto-reverts when you leave the game. *Entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall. Install over 2.9.7; everything carries over.*

releases.name: Bannerlator 2.9.7
releases.body:
# Bannerlator 2.9.7 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **2.9.7 is a small, focused update over 2.9.6** — a big controller-reliability overhaul plus a Task Manager fix, landing incrementally on the **road to 3.0**. Everything from 2.9.6 is included. As always it's **entirely app-side** — **no ImageFS reinstall** — your containers, themes, custom accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. Install straight over 2.9.6. ## 🎮 Controller reliability overhaul The headline of 2.9.7 — controllers that stay connected and land on the right player. - **Hot-plug that actually holds** — physical controllers survive mid-game reconnects and Bluetooth sleep/wake without dropping, via stable **descriptor-keyed player slots** and debounced reconnect handling. - **On-screen controls no longer die** — the touch / on-screen gamepad used to stop responding after ~15 minutes; a rewritten input transport (a shared-memory ring buffer) fixes that at the root. - **No more stolen Player 1** — handheld "extra" input devices (such as the AYANEO's aux buttons) were grabbing Player 1; a **capability filter** now only counts real gamepads, so your actual controller stays Player 1. - **Player Slots — assign who's who** — a new **Players** panel lets you pin each controller (and the on-screen pad) to a specific **Player 1–4**, or **Auto / Ignore**. Available live in-game, and out-of-game per-container and per-game. Includes **shared-slot** control (two devices driving one player) and **on-screen auto-yield** (hand Player 1 to a real pad when it connects). - **Controller-status toast** — a brief on-screen card shows each detected controller and its assigned player on launch and whenever assignments change, so you can confirm the mapping without opening a tester. - **Reset Input** — one tap re-initializes the whole input pipeline without relaunching the game. - Every option carries a **"?" explanation**. ## 🧠 Free Memory — honest and effective The "Free memory" action is now **two clearly labeled tiers**: a light **Drop file caches** (what the old button actually did), and a root-only **Deep clean** that force-stops background apps to free real RAM — while **sparing your running game and system apps**. There's also an optional **auto deep-clean on launch**. ## 🧩 Task Manager — Processor Affinity now reflects your choice Setting a process's **Processor Affinity** always took effect, but the dialog used to reopen showing **all cores checked** — it wasn't reading back the cores you'd picked. It now shows your real selection every time you reopen it. > 🔜 **Coming next:** a deeper affinity fix — pinning *every* worker thread of the process, not just most — is already written and lands in a following release. See the road to 3.0 below. ## 🛣️ On the road to 3.0 2.9.7 is a deliberate step toward a smooth **3.0**, landing pieces incrementally so each is proven on real devices before the big version bump: - **Processor Affinity — Part 2** — the in-guest helper gets rebuilt to pin every worker thread, closing the small gap where a few threads could drift back onto disabled cores. - More controller and stability polish building on the overhaul above. 3.0 rolls these up once each is device-proven — no big-bang surprises. ## ➕ Everything from 2.9.6, carried forward All of 2.9.6 is included — the **portrait container-editor tabs**, **backgrounded games staying alive** (foreground service), **Turnip GMEM / TU_DEBUG** tuning, the **cross-vendor performance HUD**, **"?" help + glossary everywhere**, bundled **AIO Graphics Test 2.0.1 / Banner File Manager 1.2.0 / Pale Moon**, the **D7VK** DirectDraw→Vulkan wrapper (bundled + catalog), and the **IPv4 DNS** container fix. ## 📦 Where to get Proton 9 The APK does not bundle Proton 9 — Wine installs from the in-app catalog on first run. > ⚠️ **A fresh install ships with no Wine at all.** On first run, open **Containers → the download icon** and install a Proton before creating a container. Updating from 2.9.6 changes nothing — your existing containers and Wine installs are untouched. **Proton 9.0 — not bundled; grab whichever matches your setup (both also appear in the in-app catalog):** **arm64ec** (default for most devices): **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-arm64ec.wcp** 66.7 MB · sha256 `f8a99fed387f1b097009129dc49368c8f500927640a9d4c7a192d850b1b2068c` **x86_64**: **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-x86_64.wcp** 50.7 MB · sha256 `ec90286b2b266aaa9dd4c5265383a48f05ccc96890d078cb3529e78b89cba2ea` Install via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. *(Compiled as wcps by **Xnick417x**.)*

 

## 🙏 Credits - **Controller reliability overhaul** — built on the controller-detection work across the community forks: - **WinNative** — the shared-memory input transport and the descriptor-keyed player-slot design our hot-plug is built on. - **palazos** (`winlatorCmod`, `controller-detection-fix`) — the hot-plug reconnect hooks, in the **brunodev85 Winlator** → **Pipetto-crypto `winlator_bionic`** lineage the fix originates from. - **[GameNative](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative)** — the progressive input-device capability handling folded into the hot-plug path. - **isygold** — **[Vegas DXVK](https://github.com/isygold/vegas-releases)**, the community DXVK builds so much of our performance rides on. - **Xnick417x** — the Proton 9.0 arm64ec + x86_64 `.wcp`s linked above. - Everyone filing **Mali reports** and issues with logs attached — the cross-vendor HUD and Mali paths keep getting proven on real hardware. - And everyone reporting, testing build after build, and adding games and configs to BannerHub & Bannerlator. ❤️ --- > ℹ️ **Root is only needed for the root-gated performance tier** (governor / CPU-clock / thermal / fan) and the new **Deep clean** memory tier. Everything else — including **non-root GPU max-clock** on Adreno — needs no root. The root tier stays opt-in, gated behind an explicit "use at your own risk" agreement, and every change auto-reverts when you leave the game. *Entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall. Install over 2.9.6; everything carries over.*

releases.name: Bannerlator 2.9.6
releases.body:
# Bannerlator 2.9.6 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **2.9.6 is a feature-and-fixes release over 2.9.5**, headlined by a rebuilt **in-game Task Manager** (per-process CPU affinity + live telemetry), a new **D7VK** wrapper that runs old **DirectX 7 / DirectDraw** games on Vulkan, a container-editor layout that stops wasting portrait space, and games that **no longer get killed when you switch away**. Everything from 2.9.5 is included. As always it's **entirely app-side** — **no ImageFS reinstall** — your containers, themes, custom accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. Install straight over 2.9.5. ## 🧰 In-game Task Manager — now a real control panel The in-game Task Manager grew from a plain process list into a proper control panel: - **Per-process Processor Affinity** — a Windows-style "Set affinity" on any running process's ⋮ menu. Pin a process to specific CPU cores **live, mid-game**, exactly like Windows Task Manager. The core toggles match the container/game core-picker (bordered tiles in one shaded panel), and it applies instantly via the guest's real affinity path — no relaunch. - **A live telemetry header** — CPU & GPU usage **and temperatures**, GPU clock, **FPS (+ minimum)**, RAM, swap, and battery (level / watts / temperature / charging), laid out as a clean stat-tile grid, plus a **per-core clock strip** (full MHz). The readings use the same cross-vendor sensors as the performance HUD. - **A container panel** — a collapsible summary of the running container's Wine/Proton, DX wrapper, renderer, graphics driver, resolution and device. > ℹ️ **Which readings are available varies from device to device.** Several values (GPU load / clock, the temperatures, and battery watts) depend on the sensors your manufacturer chooses to expose — on some hardware a few of these are locked down and will simply read **"—"**. That's a device/vendor constraint, not a bug. ## 🎮 D7VK — DirectX 7 / DirectDraw games on Vulkan Old **DirectDraw / Direct3D 3–7** titles historically took a slow OpenGL path. **D7VK** (WinterSnowfall's Vulkan implementation, a DXVK cousin) runs them straight through **Vulkan** instead: - New **D7VK** option in the **DDraw Wrapper** picker — available **per-container and per-game**. - Ships **bundled** and offline-ready as the **default**, and is now **catalog-backed**: select **D7VK** and a **"D7VK Version"** dropdown + download button appears, letting you pull **bleeding-edge nightly d7vk builds** straight from the catalog and switch between them. - Entirely app-side — the wrapper drops into the container at launch, **no ImageFS reinstall**, and existing containers can use it immediately. ## 🧭 Container editor — tabs back on top in portrait The landscape rail was great in landscape but cramped in portrait. Now the editor adapts to the orientation: - **Portrait** — the tabs (General / Environment / Drives / Win Components / Advanced) sit in a single **icon bar across the top**, spread evenly across the full width, with the **?** help (and **Reset** on the defaults screen) tucked at the end of that row. Content gets the full width underneath, and the wasted band at the top is gone. - **Landscape** — unchanged: the collapsible left rail you already know. - Applies to all three container screens — **New Container**, **Edit Container**, and **New Container Defaults**. ## 🛡️ Backgrounded games stay alive Switching to another app (or getting a call) mid-game used to let Android quietly kill the container. 2.9.6 runs the game session as a **real foreground service** with a persistent notification, so a backgrounded game or container **keeps running** instead of being evicted. Come back and it's still there. ## 🎛️ Deeper graphics tuning (Turnip) - **GMEM control (Auto / On / Off)** for Adreno (710 / 720 / 722) — force tiled rendering on or off, per-container **and** per-game. - **Advanced `TU_DEBUG` tokens** (concurrent-binning force/off, deck-emu, and more) for squeezing out compatibility and performance on tricky titles. - Every option carries a **"?" explanation** and a glossary entry so you know what it actually does before you flip it. ## 📟 Performance HUD — wider device support + honest API labels - **Cross-vendor metrics** — the HUD now reads GPU load / clock and charging state on **MediaTek (GED)** and other non-Adreno devices, not just Adreno. - **App-declared graphics API** — apps that report their active API (e.g. the bundled AIO Graphics Test's per-backend tests) now show the **correct** API in the HUD instead of a best guess. ## ❓ "?" help everywhere + glossary Per-option **"?" help buttons** now cover **every technical setting** across the container editor, the per-game shortcut editor, and the Turnip / Wrapper driver config — each backed by a plain-language **glossary** ("What is all this?"). No more guessing what a toggle does. ## 📦 Bundled in every container New and existing containers pick these up automatically (no reinstall): - **[AIO Graphics Test 2.0.1](https://github.com/The412Banner/AIO-Graphics-Test/releases/tag/2.0.1)** ([repo](https://github.com/The412Banner/AIO-Graphics-Test)) — a single-window multi-API graphics test / benchmark with an **automatic OpenGL fallback** for Mali / broken-DXVK setups (a separate "AIO Graphics Test (OpenGL)" Start-menu entry is there as a safety net). - **[Banner File Manager 1.2.0](https://github.com/The412Banner/banner-file-manager/releases/tag/v1.2.0)** ([repo](https://github.com/The412Banner/banner-file-manager)) — faster on large folders, with version metadata. - **[Pale Moon](https://www.palemoon.org/)** — a lightweight browser, launchable from the container **Start Menu**. ## 🌐 Container networking fix Containers now get a **usable IPv4 DNS resolver**, fixing games and launchers that couldn't resolve hostnames. ## 🐛 Fixes - **New containers show up immediately** in the Games "add a game" container picker — no more launching or restarting the app first to make a just-created container appear. - **Pale Moon** no longer clutters the container desktop or the Games tab — it lives in the Start Menu only. - Assorted stability and UI polish. ## ➕ Everything from 2.9.5, carried forward All of 2.9.5 is included — **Unpack Archive** (ISO/RAR/7z/GOG-installer/native FreeArc repack extraction right in the File Manager), the **landscape UI overhaul** (collapsible rails + App Orientation), **frame-generation present modes** (auto-mailbox during FG, live Present Mode selector, bionic-fg re-enabled), and the GL/Zink perf-HUD FPS fix. ## 🔜 Coming soon Already scoped and on the way in an upcoming update: - **Controller hot-plug & reconnection** — controllers that drop mid-game (Bluetooth sleep/wake, a knocked-loose cable, a flaky dongle) will **reconnect cleanly on their own** instead of going dead until you relaunch the game. This targets the reported controller disconnect / drop issues (**#221**). - **More D7VK nightlies** — bleeding-edge d7vk builds keep landing in the in-app catalog as upstream evolves. ## 📦 Where to get Proton 9 The APK does not bundle Proton 9 — Wine installs from the in-app catalog on first run. > ⚠️ **A fresh install ships with no Wine at all.** On first run, open **Containers → the download icon** and install a Proton before creating a container. Updating from 2.9.5 changes nothing — your existing containers and Wine installs are untouched. **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** — not bundled, download it if you want it: **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-arm64ec.wcp** 66.7 MB · sha256 `f8a99fed387f1b097009129dc49368c8f500927640a9d4c7a192d850b1b2068c` Install it via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. It also appears in the in-app catalog. *(Compiled as a wcp by **Xnick417x**.)* **Proton 9.0 x86-64** — for **x86-64** containers, not bundled: **https://github.com/StevenMXZ/Winlator-Contents/releases/download/1.0/Proton.9.0-x86_64.wcp** 50.7 MB · sha256 `ec90286b2b266aaa9dd4c5265383a48f05ccc96890d078cb3529e78b89cba2ea` Install it the same way via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. *(Provided by **StevenMXZ** — [Winlator-Contents](https://github.com/StevenMXZ/Winlator-Contents).)*

 

## 🙏 Credits - **[WinterSnowfall — d7vk](https://github.com/WinterSnowfall/d7vk)** — the Vulkan implementation of D3D3–7 that powers the new D7VK wrapper. - **[GameNative](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative)** — the frame-generation groundwork and present-pacing lineage Bannerlator's FG rides on. - **isygold** — **[Vegas DXVK](https://github.com/isygold/vegas-releases)**, the community DXVK builds so much of our performance rides on. - **Xnick417x** — the working **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** `.wcp` linked above. - **[StevenMXZ](https://github.com/StevenMXZ/Winlator-Contents)** — the **Proton 9.0 x86-64** `.wcp` linked above. - Everyone filing **Mali reports** and issues with logs attached — the Mali BCn path and cross-vendor HUD were both proven out on real hardware. - And everyone reporting, testing build after build, and adding games and configs to BannerHub & Bannerlator. ❤️ --- > ℹ️ **Root is only needed for the root-gated performance tier** (governor / CPU-clock / thermal / fan). Everything else — including **non-root GPU max-clock** on Adreno — needs no root. The root tier stays opt-in, gated behind an explicit "use at your own risk" agreement, and every change auto-reverts when you leave the game. *Entirely app-side — no ImageFS reinstall. Install over 2.9.5; everything carries over.*

releases.body: # Bannerlator 2.9.5 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **2.9.5 is a feature release over 2.9.4**, headlined by a brand-new **Unpack Archive** tool that installs games right in the File Manager, and a full **landscape UI overhaul**. Everything from 2.9.4 is included. As always it's **entirely app-side** — **no ImageFS reinstall** — your containers, themes, custom accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. Install straight over 2.9.4. ## 📦 Unpack Archive — install games right in the File Manager A brand-new extractor built into the File Manager (**⋮ → Unpack**, or one-tap **Fast Extract**): - **Archives & disc images** — **ISO/UDF**, ZIP, RAR, 7z, and the **TAR family** (GZ/XZ/BZ2/ZST), all via a bundled 7-Zip engine. No external tools, and the kernel can't loop-mount these on Android anyway. - **GOG installers** — pull the game straight out of `setup_*.exe` with a bundled **innoextract**. No need to run the installer under Wine first. - **Native FreeArc repack install — no PC!** FitGirl / DODI-style **FreeArc** repacks (LZMA / tornado / rep) now decompress **on-device** via a bundled NDK `unarc`. *(srep-based repacks still need a Windows PC — the app tells you and offers the container route.)* - **Fast Extract** — one tap unpacks to a new folder straight into a **minimizable progress pill** with a **foreground notification**, so multi-hour extracts survive being backgrounded (yes, even on HONOR). - **Content-aware ⋮ menu** — offers Unpack on any real archive regardless of extension (including `.wcp`), with **power / thread** and **read-buffer** controls and battery-kill hardening. ## 🖥️ Landscape UI overhaul Landscape stopped wasting the top and bottom of the screen: - **Tabs → a collapsible left rail** on the Container editors, File Manager, and Save Manager — reclaiming the vertical height the horizontal tab bar was eating. - The rail collapses to icons (with tiny labels in portrait), **remembers its state per-screen**, and **reflows on rotation** without losing your tab, edits, or scroll. - **File Manager** — a left **Locations rail** (Internal / SD / Downloads / Games / favourites), **grid** by default in landscape (and the grid/list toggle now works in **portrait** too), **New Folder** moved into the toolbar, and outlined selectors. - **Save Manager** — a left Steam / Custom / Settings rail, **multi-column** game cards, and a sync-count **badge + banner**. - **Container editors** — the collapsible rail, reclaimed bottom space, and the **Wine-glass** container glyph on the rail. - A **slim top header** on every screen. - A new **App Orientation** setting (Auto / Portrait / Landscape) locks the app UI to an orientation — **games are unaffected**. ## 🎞️ Frame Generation & Present Modes - Fixed frame-gen being strangled by FIFO backpressure — it now **forces mailbox while FG multiplies**, and **bionic-fg is re-enabled** (device-verified). - A live in-game **Present Mode selector** on the Graphics tab (FG gated to the **Vulkan** renderer). - Both **bionic-fg** and **lsfg-vk** are offered; treat them as experimental and use whichever works best for your game. ## 🐛 Fixes - **GL/Zink perf-HUD now reads real FPS** (it was stuck at 0.0) — it counts on the child render surface the game actually presents to. - File Manager grid/list toggle works in portrait, plus assorted landscape UI polish. ## 📦 Where to get Proton 9 The APK does not bundle Proton 9 — Wine installs from the in-app catalog on first run. > ⚠️ **A fresh install ships with no Wine at all.** On first run, open **Containers → the download icon** and install a Proton before creating a container. releases.name: Bannerlator 2.9.4
releases.body:
# Bannerlator 2.9.4 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **2.9.4 is a feature release over 2.9.3**, headlined by a **HUD overhaul** — the Fusion overlay becomes the default and gains a live on/off switch — plus a batch of **container-setup quality-of-life** and the fix for the **log-storage crash that was closing games mid-play**. Everything from 2.9.3 is included. As always it's **entirely app-side** — **no ImageFS reinstall** — your containers, themes, custom accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. Install straight over 2.9.3. ## 🎚️ HUD overhaul — Fusion by default, with an on/off switch The in-game performance overlay got a proper pass. - **Fusion is now the default HUD**, at its compact **Pill** size, and it gained a system-wide **RAM%** readout alongside the existing GPU/CPU/battery lines. - **A master "Show HUD" toggle.** The FPS tab in the side menu now opens with a single switch that turns the whole overlay **on or off live** — no relaunch. Your **frame-rate and refresh** controls stay put at the top (they're not part of the overlay, so turning the HUD off never touches your frame cap). - **Tidy, collapsible sections.** The rest of the appearance settings — **Style & Size, Metrics, Appearance, Alerts, Tools** — collapse into tap-to-open sections instead of one long scroll, closed by default and hidden entirely while the HUD is off. - A thin **accent line** now separates the tab buttons from their content, following your theme accent. ## 🗂️ Log storage moved to Documents — fixes games closing mid-play Logs used to default to the app's private **`Android/data`** folder, which lives on Android's restricted-FUSE storage. Under heavy logging, the keep-last-N **log rotation** — deleting old logs while a game still had them open — could **crash the phone's media-storage service**, and Android would respond by **killing the running game or container**. That showed up as the maddening "**the game just closes**" mid-play (worst on the **pubg** build and the **AYANEO Pocket FIT**). Logs now default to **`Documents/bannerlator`**, an ordinary public folder that avoids that path, and the crash-prone **"App data"** option is **removed** so nobody can land back on it. Existing installs are **migrated automatically** — nothing to change, and your logs are easier to find and share in a file manager now too. ## 🧰 Easier container setup - **New Container Defaults — now yours to set, per architecture.** A settings cog on the Games/Containers bar opens the container editor in a "defaults" mode; save it and every new container seeds from your profile. Because the emulator/box64/FEXCore stack is architecture-coupled, defaults are kept **independently for x86-64 and arm64ec** — a new container seeds from the profile matching its Wine's architecture. - **"What is all this?" — a newcomer glossary.** A plain-English glossary (34 terms) plus a **?** on individual fields explains what every container setting actually does, so the editor stops being a wall of jargon. - **Environment-variable editor fixes.** Custom variables are **no longer silently dropped on save**, the Add dialog now has separate **Name** and **Value** fields, and the recognized-variable catalog grew from ~34 to **~75** (the full BCn/Mali family included). - **Save Manager — custom Restore, any time.** Restoring a save into a custom (imported EXE/folder) game is now **always available**, through the in-app file picker. ## 🧩 Mali — BCn→ASTC transcode on the default driver BCn texture transcode is now available on the **default** compute path, for **any** wrapper — including "Original", which has no built-in BCn of its own. It's done by a bundled standalone Vulkan layer, not the wrapper's own code. A companion fix also stops a **double BCn decode** (the compute layer and a wrapper's own emulation both transcoding the same texture), which was producing corrupt or black textures on some Mali setups. > **On Mali:** open the graphics driver settings, set **BCn Emulation Type = Compute**, then enable **BCn → ASTC**. On **Adreno** the option is inert — Adreno decodes BCn natively. ## 🔤 Polish & fixes - The **"+" add button** on Games and Containers no longer lands **off-screen in right-to-left languages** ([#200](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/issues/200)). The tell was a mirrored layout even with English text — thanks **@aszba258-cyber** and **@alroe2435-cell** for reporting, and **iManiii** for verifying the fix on device. - Landscape **dialog scroll / clipping** fixes across the growable pickers and the Select-container dialogs, so long lists are reachable in landscape. ## ⚠️ Frame generation — use lsfg-vk **bionic-fg** stays **temporarily disabled** in Frame Generation — after dozens of discussions it remained a work-in-progress and kept drawing false-positive "it's working" reports. Use **lsfg-vk** for now; it comes back as selectable once it's proven to work as intended. > **lsfg-vk is experimental.** It's the recommended frame-gen option today, but results vary by title and hardware — **don't expect it to run fluidly on every game and every device.** ## ➕ Everything from 2.9.3, carried forward All of 2.9.3 is included — the full **Save Manager** (Steam Cloud two-way sync, cloud-honesty local backups, Auto-Collect, the universal vault for custom games), the smoother **lsfg-vk** frame-gen defaults, the hardened **Perf HUD**, and everything from **2.9.2**, **2.9.1** and **2.9**. ## 📦 Where to get Proton 9 The APK does not bundle Proton 9 — Wine installs from the in-app catalog on first run. > ⚠️ **A fresh install ships with no Wine at all.** On first run, open **Containers → the download icon** and install a Proton before creating a container. Updating from 2.9.3 changes nothing — your existing containers and Wine installs are untouched. **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** — not bundled, download it if you want it: **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-arm64ec.wcp** 66.7 MB · sha256 `f8a99fed387f1b097009129dc49368c8f500927640a9d4c7a192d850b1b2068c` Install it via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. It also appears in the in-app catalog. *(Compiled as a wcp by **Xnick417x**.)*

 

## 🙏 Credits - **[GameNative](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative)** — the lsfg-vk frame-generation defaults and the present-pacing groundwork Bannerlator's FG rides on. - **isygold** — **[Vegas DXVK](https://github.com/isygold/vegas-releases)**, the community DXVK builds so much of our performance rides on. - **@aszba258-cyber**, **@alroe2435-cell** and **iManiii** — reporting and verifying the RTL "+" button fix (#200). - Everyone filing **Mali reports** and issues with logs attached — the Mali BCn path and the log-storage fix were both proven out on real hardware. - **Xnick417x** — the working **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** `.wcp` linked above. - And everyone reporting, testing build after build, and adding games and configs to BannerHub & Bannerlator. ❤️ --- > ℹ️ **Root is only needed for the root-gated performance tier** (governor/CPU-clock/thermal/fan). Everything else — including **non-root GPU max-clock** on Adreno — needs no root. The root tier stays opt-in, gated behind an explicit "use at your own risk" agreement, and every change auto-reverts when you leave the game.

releases.name: Bannerlator 2.9.3
releases.body:
> ## 🎉 2,000 members & 400,000+ downloads — thank you > > Two milestones landed at once. Our Discord has officially crossed **2,000 members**, and Bannerlator — only **45 days old**, first commit June 18th — has already passed **400,000 downloads**. None of this is mine; it's **ours**. To everyone who reports bugs, tests build after build, adds games and configs to BannerHub & Bannerlator, and especially everyone on **Mali devices** that we're still working out and adjusting for daily — **thank you.** The app is still young and there are absolutely still bugs to iron out; I appreciate your patience and everyone debugging right alongside me. This is only the beginning. 🚀 # Bannerlator 2.9.3 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **2.9.3 is a feature release over 2.9.2**, headlined by a full **Save Manager** — one screen built so you never lose a game save again. It also retunes **lsfg-vk frame generation** to smoother, faster defaults out of the box, and hardens the in-game performance HUD. Everything from 2.9.2 is included. As always it's **entirely app-side** — **no ImageFS reinstall** — your containers, themes, custom accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. Install straight over 2.9.2. ## 💾 Save Manager — Steam Cloud sync + never lose a save A whole screen dedicated to protecting and moving your game saves — reach it from the **side menu** (under Library), the **Steam store** toolbar, or any game's **⋮ menu** or detail page. - **Three tiers, kept in sync.** It manages your saves across **Steam Cloud**, your local **Library**, and the **container** (the per-game Windows prefix), and moves them between those places for you — uploads are **incremental** (only the files that actually changed). - **Steam Cloud sync — both directions.** Pull a game's saves **down from Steam Cloud** into any container, so a title you played on another device (or before a reinstall) picks up right where you left off — then push your local progress **back up to the cloud**, **incrementally** (only the files that actually changed). It reads each game's real Steam Cloud layout (UFS config) to map saves to the correct place instead of guessing, so it's genuine two-way sync, not just a local copy. - **Cloud honesty.** Some games advertise Steam Cloud but don't actually *keep* your saves there (FlatOut 2 is the poster child). The Save Manager checks for this and, when a game's cloud won't retain your files, **backs them up locally instead and tells you plainly** — no silent "uploaded" that vanishes later. - **Auto-Collect.** Turn it on and your saves are grabbed automatically **when you exit a game** and **before you uninstall** one — so removing a game never takes your progress with it. Per-type toggles and clear confirm/info prompts keep you in control. - **A universal vault for custom games too.** It isn't Steam-only. Any **imported EXE or folder game** gets the same backup, restore, and **auto-snapshot on exit**, stored in per-game folders under `Downloads/Bannerlator/game saves/` — and you can **restore a save into whichever container you choose**. - **Nothing slips through.** A **"played but never synced"** flag surfaces games you've run but never backed up, and a live **Steam connection badge + auto-connect** means the manager wires itself up the moment you open it. - **Safe by design.** It only ever touches files it created, and restores go exactly where you point them. **📖 Want the full picture?** Read the complete, plain-English walkthrough: **[Save Manager — Complete Guide](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/blob/main/docs/save-manager-guide.md).** ## 🎞️ Frame generation — smoother by default (lsfg-vk) The **lsfg-vk** frame-generation defaults are retuned to match the settings that get the best real-world results on mobile GPUs — the same ones the wider scene has landed on: - **Performance mode is now ON by default** — a lighter interpolation model that costs the GPU less, which on Adreno is the difference between frame-gen *raising* your FPS and it dragging the base rate down. - **Flow scale defaults higher (0.80)** for cleaner motion and fewer artifacts on the generated frames. - **New per-container "Auto-enable at launch" (ON by default)** — frame generation now starts **live at your saved multiplier from the very first frame**, instead of loading silently and waiting for you to switch it on in the drawer. Every one of these is still a toggle. Prefer the old behavior? Flip **Auto-enable at launch** off for that container and frame-gen goes back to starting off until you enable it in-game. *(Defaults ported from **[GameNative](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative)** — see Credits.)* ## 📊 Perf HUD — right API, right game On dual-API builds the in-game overlay now reads the **active DirectX API straight from the engine log** and pins it to the running game, so the DX version it reports is the one actually in use. ## ➕ Everything from 2.9.2, carried forward All of 2.9.2 is included — the **Log Manager off-state fix** (turning recording off now actually stops logging), and through it the whole **Log Manager** (folder-per-game, rotation, the 521-channel browser, the built-in viewer, redaction, Report a problem), **non-root GPU max clock** on Adreno, the **drawer & library controls**, **Vulkan 1.4 by default**, and everything from **2.9.1** and **2.9**. ## 📦 Where to get Proton 9 The APK does not bundle Proton 9 — Wine installs from the in-app catalog on first run. > ⚠️ **A fresh install ships with no Wine at all.** On first run, open **Containers → the download icon** and install a Proton before creating a container. Updating from 2.9.2 changes nothing — your existing containers and Wine installs are untouched. **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** — not bundled, download it if you want it: **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-arm64ec.wcp** 66.7 MB · sha256 `f8a99fed387f1b097009129dc49368c8f500927640a9d4c7a192d850b1b2068c` Install it via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. It also appears in the in-app catalog. *(Compiled as a wcp by **Xnick417x**.)*

 

## 🙏 Credits - **[GameNative](https://github.com/utkarshdalal/GameNative)** — the proven lsfg-vk frame-generation defaults adopted in this release, and the present-pacing groundwork Bannerlator's FG limiter is built on. - **isygold** — **[Vegas DXVK](https://github.com/isygold/vegas-releases)**, the community DXVK builds that so much of our performance rides on. - **D4V1Z0N** and everyone filing **Mali reports** and issues with logs attached — the Save Manager was hardened through round after round of real-device testing, and it shows. - **[@arro000](https://github.com/arro000)** — **Virtual Controller Pro** ([#156](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/pull/156)), carried forward. - **Xnick417x** — the working **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** `.wcp` linked above. - And **2,000 of you** — for the reports, the patience, the configs, and for sticking with a 45-day-old project through its rough edges. ❤️ --- > ℹ️ **Root is only needed for the root-gated performance tier** (governor/CPU-clock/thermal/fan). Everything else — including **non-root GPU max-clock** on Adreno — needs no root. The root tier stays opt-in, gated behind an explicit "use at your own risk" agreement, and every change auto-reverts when you leave the game.

releases.body:
# Bannerlator 2.9.2 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **2.9.2 is a hotfix over 2.9.1.** It fixes one thing, and it affects everyone: the Log Manager's switches never actually stopped logging. Everything from 2.9.1 is included. As always it's **entirely app-side** — **no ImageFS reinstall** — your containers, themes, custom accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. Install straight over 2.9.1. ## 🔇 Turning logging off now actually turns logging off In 2.9.1, switching every toggle in the Log Manager off did **not** stop Bannerlator writing a log. Setting `WINEDEBUG=-all` yourself didn't stop it either. The switches chose *how chatty* Wine was; nothing ever told the app to stop **writing the file**. So the log kept filling from everything else running under the hood — the x86 translator, the Wine server, the loader, DXVK — and there was no way to switch it off. **What that cost you.** When nothing is listening, Bannerlator normally throws that output away without even reading it. Because it was always listening, that never happened — so **every 2.9.1 install was writing to disk, line by line, on every launch**, whether you wanted logs or not. It was a small tax on every game you played, hidden behind a screen that told you it was optional. **Now:** with the recording switches off, no log file is opened, nothing is written, no empty per-game folders are left behind, and the output is discarded untouched — the way it always should have been. Turn a switch back on and logging resumes exactly as before. **Viewing is unaffected.** The Log Manager, the log viewer, per-game **View logs**, the File Manager, sharing and **Report a problem** all keep working on whatever's already on disk. Switching recording off only stops *new* logs being written; it never hides or deletes what you already have. > ⚠️ **One thing worth knowing.** With every recording switch off, a crash now leaves **no Wine log** — that's the point of the fix. If you hit a bug you want to report, turn **Wine debug** on, reproduce it once, then use **Report a problem**. The launch-failure screen already tells you this when logging is off. ## ➕ Everything from 2.9.1, carried forward All of 2.9.1 is included — the **Log Manager** itself (folder per game, rotation, the 521-channel browser, the built-in viewer, redaction, Report a problem), **non-root GPU max clock** on Adreno, the **drawer & library controls** (hideable side-menu sections, SD card storage card, movable **+** button, multi-select removal, four-across grid), **Vulkan 1.4 by default** with the version clamped to what your driver reports, and the **FEXCore SMC-checks** fix. And through it, all of 2.9. ## 📦 Where to get Proton 9 The APK does not bundle Proton 9 — Wine installs from the in-app catalog on first run. > ⚠️ **A fresh install ships with no Wine at all.** On first run, open **Containers → the download icon** and install a Proton before creating a container. It also appears in the in-app catalog. *(Compiled as a wcp by **Xnick417x**.)*

He then tested the fix on his own device off, on, off again and on again, and confirmed every cycle recorded and stopped correctly before it shipped. **This release is his.** - **[@arro000](https://github.com/arro000)** — **Virtual Controller Pro** ([#156](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/pull/156)), carried forward from 2.9. - **Xnick417x** — the working **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** `.wcp` linked above. - Everyone filing **Mali reports** and issues with logs attached — and everyone who reports something that looks small. releases.body:
# Bannerlator 2.9.1 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **2.9.1 is a point release over 2.9.** It adds a full **Log Manager** — so when something breaks you can capture exactly what happened and file a report with the logs already attached — plus a set of drawer and library controls, and a way to lock your GPU to max clock **without root**. Everything from 2.9 is included. As always it's **entirely app-side** — **no ImageFS reinstall** — your containers, themes, custom accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. Install straight over 2.9. ## 🗂️ Log Manager (new) One screen for everything logging: **App Settings → Logs → Open Log Manager**. - **A folder per game** with **keep-last-N rotation**, so logs from ten sessions ago stop burying the run you actually care about. Choose where they live: app data, Download, Documents, or a folder you pick. - **Pick exactly what gets recorded** — Wine debug, Box64/FEXCore, DXVK & VKD3D, Android logcat, crash reports. Every toggle has a **"?"** that **leads with what it costs you**, because two of them genuinely slow games down. - **Browse all 521 Wine debug channels** — grouped by family (graphics, sound, input, networking…) with a **"What's this?"** switch that explains each one in plain English. The 18 everyday channels stay one tap away. - **A built-in log viewer** — file tabs, a live **following** tail, severity colouring, find, wrap, copy and share. It reads only the tail of a file, so a multi-gigabyte Wine log opens instantly. - **View logs on any game** — long-press a game in grid view, or use the ⋮ menu in list view, and go straight to that game's logs. - **Report a problem** — builds a **redacted** zip of the run and opens a GitHub issue with the details already filled in: device, app version, GPU, driver, DXVK and VKD3D versions. Attach the zip and send. - **Redaction everywhere** — usernames, e-mail addresses and tokens are stripped *before* anything is written, including from crash reports and stack traces. Logcat capture is **Bannerlator's own output only** — never a system-wide capture, even with root, because that would sweep other apps' data into a file we invite you to share. > 🔒 **Your own files are safe.** Delete and "Clear all" remove **only** files Bannerlator wrote; anything else in your log folder is left alone, by construction rather than by care. ## ⚡ Lock GPU to max clock — now without root The **Lock GPU to max clock** control used to need root. On **Adreno** devices it now works with **no root at all** — on a Snapdragon handheld it took the GPU from 231 MHz to **1000 MHz** with root never granted. If you *do* have root, the original path is still used. Turning it off puts the clock back. ## 🎨 Drawer & library controls (new) - **Hide what you don't use.** **Appearance → Side Menu** now has switches for the **game stores** section (GOG, Epic, Amazon, Steam), **internal storage**, and **SD card storage** — each independently. - **SD card storage card.** The drawer's storage bar is now labelled **Internal Storage**, and if a card is in the device it gets **its own card** beneath it. - **Move the + button.** **Long-press it and slide it along the bottom** of Games or Containers, so it stops covering a card's play or ⋮ button. It stays where you put it. - **Multi-select removal.** A new button in the Games header lets you select several games — in list *or* grid — and remove them in one go. - **A four-across grid.** A third view mode: list, the original grid, and a new compact grid that fits four covers per row. ## 🔧 Graphics & runtime - **Vulkan 1.4 by default**, with the exported version **clamped to the minor your driver actually reports** — picking 1.4 on a 1.3 driver used to produce a version string no driver would accept. - **Non-Adreno GPUs** now default new containers to **wrapper-gamenative**. - **FEXCore:** the SMC-checks variable was being set under the wrong name (`FEX_SMC_CHECKS`); it is `FEX_SMCCHECKS`, so that setting now actually applies. ## 📦 Smaller install — and where to get Proton 9 The APK is **~103 MB smaller**: the bundled Proton 9 has been removed, because that bundled copy never launched. Wine now installs from the in-app catalog on first run. > ⚠️ **A fresh install ships with no Wine at all.** On first run, open **Containers → the download icon** and install a Proton before creating a container. Updating from 2.9 changes nothing — your existing containers and Wine installs are untouched. **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** — not bundled, download it if you want it: **https://github.com/The412Banner/Nightlies/releases/download/Proton/wine/proton-9.0-arm64ec.wcp** 66.7 MB · sha256 `f8a99fed387f1b097009129dc49368c8f500927640a9d4c7a192d850b1b2068c` Install it via **Containers → download icon → install the `.wcp`**. It also appears in the in-app catalog. *(Compiled as a wcp by **Xnick417x**.)* ## ➕ Everything from 2.9, carried forward All of 2.9 is included — the **Power-user Performance** controls and the opt-in root tier, **Virtual Controller Pro**, the **Mali GPU report board**, the **Fusion HUD** and cross-vendor metrics, **frame generation**, the **FPS limiter**, **Community Configs** + accounts, the **File Manager** overhaul, **Smart Game Import**, in-game refresh-rate unlock, custom startup services, and driver-source management.

 

## 🙏 Credits - **[@arro000](https://github.com/arro000)** — **Virtual Controller Pro** ([#156](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/pull/156)), carried forward from 2.9. - **Xnick417x** — the working **Proton 9.0 arm64ec** `.wcp` linked above. - Everyone filing **Mali reports** and issues with logs attached — [#193](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/issues/193) is exactly why the Log Manager exists. --- > ℹ️ **Root is only needed for the root-gated performance tier** (governor/CPU-clock/thermal/fan). Everything else — including the new **non-root GPU max-clock** on Adreno — needs no root. The root tier stays opt-in, gated behind an explicit "use at your own risk" agreement, and every change auto-reverts when you leave the game.

releases.body:
# Bannerlator 2.9 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **2.9 is a big feature release** — it adds a full **Power-user Performance** control set (safe boosts for everyone, plus a root-gated hardware-tuning tier) and finalizes **Virtual Controller Pro**, a complete on-screen controls overhaul. Everything from 2.8.x is included. As always it's **entirely app-side** — **no ImageFS reinstall** — your containers, themes, custom accent and per-game settings carry over untouched. Just install over any 2.8.x build. ## ⚡ Power-user Performance controls (new) A new **Performance** section — reachable from **App Settings → Performance** *and* the **in-game Debug tab**, kept in two-way sync — with global defaults and optional per-game overrides. **No root required (everyone):** - **Sustained Performance Mode** — keeps clocks steady instead of spiking and dropping, so long sessions stay smoother. - **Thread Priority Boost** — raises the game's CPU-worker threads so they get more time. - **Prefer Big Cores** — pins the running game to your device's fastest cores. **Root-gated tier (opt-in, Magisk / KernelSU / APatch):** locked behind a **"Grant Root"** gate with a scroll-to-accept **"use at your own risk"** disclaimer — - CPU governor → performance, **Lock CPU frequency to max**, **Keep all cores online**, **Lock GPU to max clock**, **Disable thermal throttling**, **Fan to maximum**, and a **"Free memory now"** action. **Built safe by default:** - **Puts your device back exactly as it found it** — every changed setting is restored to its precise original value automatically when you exit a game, background the app, or if it crashes (and it self-repairs on next launch after a hard kill). - A device-anchored **Temperature Watchdog** — it reads your device's *own* thermal limits and rolls settings back before it overheats. Presets: **Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive / Manual**. - Full in-app help — a **"?"** on every toggle, an **"Explain toggles"** overview, a watchdog explainer, and live CPU/GPU temps + your device's own thermal limits shown inline. Tune it before launching (App Settings) or live from the in-game Debug tab. The root tier is entirely optional and gated behind the risk disclaimer. ## 🎮 Virtual Controller Pro (new) The on-screen controls editor has been completely reworked — a redesigned editor with a dedicated **settings pane** and **toolbar**, **control scale up to 300%**, richer **visual styles**, and improved **external-controller** handling. Build and tune touch layouts far more precisely than before. *(Thanks [@arro000](https://github.com/arro000) — [#156](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/pull/156).)* ## 🐛 New: Mali GPU issue report board Mali-GPU users now have a dedicated place to report games that don't work — a **structured report form** and **public forum threads** so issues are tracked and discussed instead of lost. Every report gets its own public discussion thread where the developers answer directly.

 

- **📝 [File a Mali game report](https://the412banner.github.io/Bannerlator/mali-reports/)** — a quick form; attach your log file(s) so we can actually help. - **📋 [Browse all reports & dev answers](https://the412banner.github.io/Bannerlator/mali-reports/reports.html)** — see what's been reported, answered, and fixed. ## ➕ Everything from 2.8.x, carried forward All of the 2.8 line is included — the **Fusion HUD** and cross-vendor performance metrics, **frame generation** (bionic-fg / lsfg-vk) with a Performance mode, the **FPS limiter**, **Community Configs** + accounts, the **File Manager** overhaul, **Smart Game Import**, background component downloads, in-game refresh-rate unlock, custom startup services, and driver-source management. ## 🙏 Credits - **[@arro000](https://github.com/arro000)** — **Virtual Controller Pro** ([#156](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/pull/156)): the reworked on-screen controls editor. - Community testers who device-verified the new Performance controls on real hardware. --- > ℹ️ **Root is only needed for the root-gated performance tier** (governor/clock/thermal/fan). Everything else in Bannerlator — including the non-root Performance boosts — needs no root. The root tier is opt-in, gated behind an explicit "use at your own risk" agreement, and every change auto-reverts when you leave the game.

releases.name: Bannerlator 2.8.2
releases.body:
# Bannerlator 2.8.2 Run Windows apps and games on Android — no PC and no root required. **2.8.2 is a small hotfix over 2.8.1** — it corrects battery power reporting on devices that report battery current in **milliamps** (e.g. the **HONOR Magic** line) and sharpens the in-game performance HUD's accuracy. Everything from 2.8.1 is included. Like always it's **entirely app-side** — **no ImageFS reinstall** — your containers, themes, custom accent and per-game settings all carry over untouched. Just install over 2.8.1. ## 🔧 What's fixed - **Battery power (Watts) now reads correctly on devices that report battery current in mA** (e.g. HONOR Magic 7 Pro) — was showing `0.0W`. Current-unit is now auto-detected (mA vs µA), so watts are right on those devices while unchanged everywhere else. - **HUD engine/API label is now live and accurate** — it re-checks the running game continuously instead of latching on the first API, so DirectX 12 / Vulkan / DirectX games (e.g. UE titles) are labeled correctly rather than stuck on the wrong one. - **Per-core CPU %** now fills in on devices where the kernel restricts per-core stats (falls back to a clock-based estimate). - **FPS reads honestly at rest** — the counter decays to 0 when no frame is being presented instead of freezing on the last number (fixes stuck FPS at menus and after switching API in the AIO Graphics Test). - **HUD stays visible on OpenGL titles** — it now follows the focused game window and re-binds correctly across API switches. ## 🙏 Credits - **Angel** — community tester on a **HONOR Magic 7 Pro** who reported the `0.0W` battery bug, ran every diagnostic and test build, and device-verified the fix. - The **[winlator_ludashi_plus](https://github.com/squalle0nhart/winlator_ludashi_plus)** project by **squalle0nhart** — its battery-current handling showed the mA-vs-µA auto-detect approach we adopted. > ## ⚠️ Testing a 2.9 pre-release (2.9-pre1 / 2 / 3 / 4)? Read this before updating. > These pre-releases carried the **Virtual Controller Pro** update (PR [#156](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/pull/156)) that you've been testing. **2.8.2 does NOT include it** — so updating to 2.8.2 will **remove your Virtual Controller Pro setups / profiles**. > > **If you want to keep those controller settings, do NOT update to 2.8.2.** Stay on your pre-release and **wait for the coming 2.9 release** (landing in the next few days), which brings Virtual Controller Pro back — finalized. Everyone else can update freely. ## 🧩 The Fusion HUD is open source — for other projects to adopt The performance overlay in this release (and the cross-vendor metric backend behind it) lives in its own **forkable, GPL-3.0 library** so any Winlator / Wine / PC-emulation project can incorporate it — including the mA/µA battery fix from this release. - 📦 **Latest release:** [**FusionHUD v1.0**](https://github.com/The412Banner/FusionHUD/releases/tag/v1.0) — library `.aar` + a demo APK to preview it. - 📁 **Source / fork it:** [**github.com/The412Banner/FusionHUD**](https://github.com/The412Banner/FusionHUD) - Consume via JitPack (`com.github.The412Banner:FusionHUD:v1.0`) or drop the source in directly. Attribution to The412Banner is required under the license's §7(b) term — otherwise fork and ship freely.
❓ Why does OpenGL / DirectDraw FPS differ from the benchmark in the All-in-One Graphics Test?
If you run the **All-in-One Graphics Test** and notice the **HUD's FPS is lower than the benchmark's own on-screen FPS** on the **OpenGL** and **DirectDraw** cubes — that's expected, and **both numbers are correct**. They measure two different points in the rendering pipeline. **The HUD reports the *displayed* frame rate** — frames that actually reach your screen. - **Direct3D and Vulkan** games explicitly *present* every rendered frame 1:1, so the emulator can count each one. Here the HUD and the game's own counter **match** — the D3D/Vulkan cubes read their true rate. - **OpenGL and DirectDraw** run through **Zink** (OpenGL-on-Vulkan). The game renders *continuously* into a shared buffer that the compositor then samples at the **display's refresh rate** — individual frames are never presented as discrete events the emulator can count. So the benchmark's built-in counter shows how fast the game's render *loop* spins (often much higher, and uncapped), while the HUD shows how many of those frames are actually **composited to the screen** (≈ your display's refresh rate). **In short:** the benchmark counts the app's internal loop; the HUD counts the frames you actually see. This gap only shows up in *uncapped synthetic tests* like the cube — **normal, frame-limited OpenGL games read the same on both**. Surfacing the true internal GL loop rate would require guest-side (Wine/Zink) instrumentation, a much deeper layer; the HUD deliberately stays on the honest *displayed* rate.
--- ## 🐛 New: Mali GPU report board Games misbehaving on a **Mali GPU** (Exynos / Dimensity / Kirin / Helio)? There's now a dedicated public bug-report board for Mali devices — file a structured report with your logs, and get answers back from the developers in a public discussion thread on each report. - **📝 File a Mali game report:** https://the412banner.github.io/Bannerlator/mali-reports/ - **📋 Browse all reports & dev answers:** https://the412banner.github.io/Bannerlator/mali-reports/reports.html Every report gets its own discussion thread — reply as the original poster (no account or password needed) and the developers answer right there.

Read this before updating. > These pre-releases carried the **Virtual Controller Pro** update (PR [#156](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/pull/156)) that you've been testing. **2.8.1 does NOT include it** — so updating to 2.8.1 will **remove your Virtual Controller Pro setups / profiles**. > > **If you want to keep those controller settings, do NOT update to 2.8.1.** Stay on your pre-release and **wait for the coming 2.9 release** (landing in the next few days), which brings Virtual Controller Pro back — finalized. Everyone else can update freely.
✨ Full feature list — click to expand everything Bannerlator offers Everything the app offers, at a glance. **🍷 Windows compatibility** - **Wine** — run native Win32/Win64 apps & games. - **Box64 / Box86** x86(-64)→ARM translation with performance presets. - **WOWBox64** for arm64ec containers. - **FEXCore** alt x86/x64 backend, with automatic unixlib (`.so`) matching per version. - **arm64ec** and **x64** container support. **🎨 Graphics & translation layers** - 📖 **[Which wrapper/driver for my device? →](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator/blob/main/docs/graphics-wrappers-guide.md)** - **DXVK** (DX8/9/10/11→Vulkan; GPLAsync & Sarek variants). - **VKD3D-Proton** (DX12→Vulkan). - **WineD3D / DirectDraw** OpenGL fallback for older titles. - **Proton bionic** layers (via GameNative) — **Proton 11.0-1** & **Proton 10.0-4** (arm64ec; FEX-unixlib + fast-yield), per-SDK (28 / 35). - **VEGAS** — Adreno-optimized DXVK (less stutter, real-time upscaling). - **Turnip / Mesa** Adreno drivers (+timeline-semaphore patches), bundled and installable. - **Wrapper Version Manager** — bring your own graphics wrapper (`.tzst`): import / update / delete, a curated **downloadable catalog** from across the Winlator family, and **auto-detected settings** for every wrapper. - **Driver-source management** *(new)* — add / remove / toggle your own adrenotools driver feeds; the built-in **MTR / WinNative Drivers** list combines MTR + WinNative-Emu releases and auto-updates. - **BCn transcoding for Mali / Xclipse** — "Wrapper + bcn_layer" driver + BCn settings panel. - **Mali DX12 (experimental)** — opt-in **"Wrapper + compat + bcn"** driver (leegao BCn + DX12 compat layer) with a **GameNative-engine** toggle, for Valhall-class Mali. **🖥️ Renderers** - **Vulkan / OpenGL / SurfaceFlinger / VirGL** host renderers. - **SurfaceFlinger colour fix** — R/B-swap + crash fix, per-container/game toggle. - **Native Rendering (Low-Latency Mode)** — direct-scanout, cuts input lag (Vulkan & OpenGL). - **Spatial upscalers** — SGSR, FSR / FSR-Fit, NIS, Sharpen (RCAS), Linear / Nearest; live in-game, saved per game. - **Fullscreen aspect modes** — Off / Fit / Stretch / Fill / Integer, live switch, per game. - **Supersampling** — 1.25× / 1.5× / 2× render scale, Lanczos-2 downsample. - **Screen effects** (Vulkan & OpenGL) — FXAA, Toon, CRT, NTSC, colour grading, CAS, fake-HDR. - **Debanding (Vulkan)** — adjustable dither pass for smooth gradients. - **ReShade** — real `.fx` effects on DXVK / VKD3D, on-device compile, ~100-effect catalog + your own, live in-game tab, per game, solo or stacked. - **VRR + in-game refresh unlock** — match refresh to FPS (Auto or 60 / 90 / 120 / 144 Hz) *and* raise the in-game refresh ceiling from the drawer where the panel/layer support it. - Adjustable resolution & frame-rate limit. **🎞️ Frame generation & pacing** - **Two engines** — Off / **bionic-fg** (bundled) / **lsfg-vk** (bring your own `Lossless.dll`), shown as a badge in-game. *(bionic-fg is temporarily non-selectable while it's proven — use lsfg-vk for now.)* - **Live controls** — Off / 2× / 3× / 4× + flow-scale slider, hot-reloaded. - **Standalone FPS limiter** — engine-independent present-pacing cap with quick 30 / 60 / 90 / 120 presets; steps aside when lsfg multiplies; both renderers. - **lsfg Performance mode** — a lighter frame-gen model for weaker GPUs; per-container and live in-game, no root required. **📦 Containers** - Multiple isolated Wine containers with redesigned spec-chip cards. - **Run as administrator** (per-container toggle) for installers/games needing elevation. - **Auto-close on game exit** (per-container toggle). - **Startup mode** — Normal / Essential / Full, plus a new **Custom** mode to pick exactly which services launch (winebus / winehid / …), defaulted per container and overridable per game. - **Import / export** containers. - Per-container Wine / driver / DXVK / VKD3D / Box64 / drives / Z-drive / env-vars, with an env-var **editor + presets** (DLL-override toggle, editable dropdowns, chip groups). - **Desktop wallpaper picker** (per-container or global). - **Compatibility Layers download menu** — browse / install / remove every component with progress bars, continuing in the background. **🕹️ Games, shortcuts & input** - Game library (grid / list, sort, filters) with redesigned cards. - **Smart Game Import** — auto-naming, SteamGridDB cover art + Steam appId identification, missing-component recommendations, and an editable **Game Details** page. - Add a single game or a **whole games folder** at once; drive letters assigned per storage volume. - **Back up / restore saves** (GameHub-compatible zips); per-game language / locale. - **On-screen touch controls** (theme-follow or per-game colour) + virtual gamepads; RTS-style touch gestures. - **Physical controllers** (SDL2) + touchpad / mouse emulation; rebuilt binding screen. - **PC-accurate vibration** — dual-motor rumble, per-container mode + intensity, winebus never-expire duration patch; per-slot **and master** toggles. - **Gyroscope motion aim** — right-stick or mouse output, Tilt-to-Aim orientation mode, Hold/Toggle activation, device calibration, saved per container and per game. **🌐 Community Configs** - **Catalog browser** (globe) with search, filters, sort, and "Matches my device". - **Matched by Steam appId** — a config resolves to the right game by its appId first (fewer wrong matches), with a **"Which game is this?"** picker for genuine ties, remembered per shortcut. - **One-tap Apply** — surgically merges just that config's settings, preserving the rest; a shared config now carries your **whole** setup (HUD layout, motion-aim, refresh cap, startup services, frame-gen model, upscaler, vibration). - **Smart install** of a config's missing DXVK / VKD3D / FEXCore / Turnip, then auto-applies. - **Config detail** — provenance, what-it-sets, before-apply diff, upvotes / downloads / comments. - **Share your own** — export the full recipe (never your files, logins or tuning), anonymous by default; **My uploads** to edit / delete. - **Optional account** (username + password, recovery-key, no email) so uploads follow you and carry your name. - **Read-only for your setup** — nothing changes unless you tap Apply. Now on **Big Picture** too, fully D-pad navigable. **🛒 Built-in stores & cross-store Download Manager** - **Steam** — user/pass or QR, owned library, built-in depot engine (JavaSteam), 4-tier speed, session hardening, DLC picker, true-size fix, optional **Goldberg** patch. - **Epic / Amazon** — sign in, browse, download / install / launch (incl.
